title: Welcome to Russia
text: {name}, a Russian citizen. Your internal passport is in your pocket, your Gosuslugi app is installed, and the metro is running. Two years ahead: study, work, fall in love, survive winter. Goals are in the side panel.

choices.then: Day 1 begins.

title: Kazansky Station, 05:40
text: {name}, the train from {home} just arrived. Migration card stamped. You have a short time to get registered (15 days for citizens of Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, 7 for most others), then a medical exam, health insurance and a patent before you can work legally. Rules change often — read everything twice.

choices.then: Cold air, Russian announcements, a stranger offering "work, registration, everything". Day 1 begins.

title: Kazansky Station, 06:10
text: {name}, citizen of an EAEU country. You need no patent to work, but you still need registration and an employment contract. Moscow is bigger than anything back in {home}.

choices.then: Day 1 begins.

title: Airport transfer to the dorm
text: {name}, a foreign student from {home}. The quota place, the dorm and the first snowflakes are real. Your student visa and registration have an expiry date — keep track of them.

choices.then: The dorm keeper hands you a key and a kettle. Day 1 begins.

title: September 1st — Day of Knowledge
text: Flowers, ribbons, first-graders with bouquets taller than them. Universities start too.

choices.then: You clap for strangers' kids. Somehow it is moving.
The library is empty and quiet.

title: Unity Day
text: A holiday, a long weekend, and everyone arguing about what it celebrates.

choices.then: Folk songs and hot sbiten.
Holiday pay is a rumour, but tips are real.

title: New Year's Eve
text: Olivier salad, tangerines, "Irony of Fate" on TV, the president's speech at midnight.

choices.then: Champagne at 00:00 and fireworks across the courtyard.

choices.t: Celebrate alone with video call home
choices.then: You make a small salad and watch the screen glow with family faces.
Double rate. The city is empty and glittery.

title: Orthodox Christmas
text: January 7th. Some neighbours go to church, others just enjoy the day off.

choices.then: Kutya and pirogi. Nobody asks for documents.
Quiet day.

title: Defender of the Fatherland Day
text: Women congratulate men, men congratulate each other, and every shop sells socks and razors.

choices.t: Buy a small gift for a colleague
choices.then: It lands well.
Day like any other.

title: International Women's Day
text: Tulips cost triple. The entire country is a flower stall.

choices.then: They smile. You pay a lot.
You still end up holding a mimosa twig.

title: Navruz
text: Spring equinox. Diaspora communities cook sumalak and gather in parks.

choices.then: Plov, music, familiar faces. For a moment Moscow feels smaller.
You eat leftovers and call {home}.

title: Victory Day, May 9
text: Parades, the Immortal Regiment, St George ribbons. Many families carry portraits of ancestors.

choices.then: Strangers share stories. Shashlik afterwards.
Fireworks over the river at 22:00.
Quiet street, lots of police in the centre.

title: Russia Day
text: June 12. Flags, concerts, a day off.

choices.then: Free tickets, dancing, ice cream.
Quiet streets, good money.

title: ЕГЭ Day
text: The Unified State Exam. Phones in a box, metal detector at the door, 3 hours 55 minutes.

choices.then: You score 0 points on the main subject.

choices.t: Skip it and try next year
choices.then: You regret it before lunch.

title: Admission results: the enrolment order
text: Applications for budget places closed on 25 July and the ranked lists came out on 27 July. Today, 7 August, the university publishes its enrolment order for the main competition. Your name was somewhere between 41 and 80 for 40 budget places.

choices.then: The lists are public, but your name is not on them: you never submitted an application on the admission portal (Online services → University application, June–July).

title: Registration — the clock is ticking
text: The rules give a short time to register your place of stay after arrival: 7 working days for most visitors; for people who come to work, 15 days for citizens of Tajikistan and Uzbekistan and 30 days for those of Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Armenia (Belarus: 90). As reported in 2024; the rules change often and the game simplifies how the days are counted. Your host, a landlord or a hostel has to submit the notice through the MFC, post office or Gosuslugi.

choices.t: Ask your landlord to submit the notice (honest)
choices.then: The landlord signs, the MFC stamps. You are registered for 90 days.
The fixer produces a valid notice. Expensive but real.
The clock keeps ticking.

title: Registration is running out
text: Your registration has less than 20 days. Renewal needs the host's consent, the migration card and the receipt.

choices.then: Number 142 in the queue, but you leave with a fresh notice.

choices.t: Pay a "helper" to jump the queue
choices.then: Done in 20 minutes for ₽3,000. The helper vanishes into the crowd.
There is always next week.

title: Medical exam for migrants
text: Before a patent you need a medical certificate: infectious diseases, drug test, fingerprinting, Russian language test. Clinics near Sakharovo are crowded.

choices.then: The system goes down at 15:00. Come back tomorrow.
The certificate is fake. It is not recognised at the MFC.

title: Patent payment
text: A work patent is paid for in monthly advance payments of income tax. In Moscow it was ₽8,900 a month in 2025 and rose to about ₽10,000 from 1 January 2026 (other regions differ). Pay on time and keep the receipts. After you receive the patent you must notify the Interior Ministry within two months.

choices.then: Receipt in hand, +30 days.
Peace of mind. +90 days.
You tell yourself you will pay on Friday.

title: You need a health insurance policy for the patent
text: To get a work patent a labour migrant must hold a voluntary health insurance policy (DMS) that covers at least ₽100,000 and lasts as long as the patent. The price in the game is an approximation: about ₽5,000 for three months. You can also buy it in Online services → Buy health insurance.

choices.then: An insurer prints a policy with your name and a hotline number. Now the patent can be bought.
You open three insurance sites and close them again.

title: Notify the Interior Ministry about your patent
text: After getting a patent you must send a notification to the Interior Ministry within two months. A friend warns: "If you forget, the patent can be suspended for a year."

choices.t: File the notification at the MFC today
choices.then: A form, a stamp and a receipt. One less thing to worry about.
The deadline does not move.

title: Your patent has been suspended
text: A clerk reads the screen: "You did not send the notification within two months. The patent is suspended for a year." Everything you do for work now counts as illegal.

choices.t: Accept it and look for another way
choices.then: You read the rules three times. A lawyer tells you: next time, mark the date in your phone.

title: Check the register of controlled persons
text: Foreigners with unresolved violations can be placed on a register of "controlled persons" with restrictions. A friend recommends checking your status on the official website.

choices.then: Your name is not on the list. You exhale.
Not knowing is not safer.

title: Unpaid fines and the bailiffs' database
text: Before certain applications, unpaid fines must be cleared. You can search the bailiffs' (FSSP) database by name and date of birth.

choices.then: A forgotten fine of ₽2,000 appears. You pay it online at once.
The fine would have grown with time.

title: Student visa extension
text: The university international office stamps the extension request. The migration service needs your attendance record.

choices.then: Approved. Visa extended for a year.
They sigh, check the list and say you are fine.

title: Working as a student?
text: Students can work only with specific permissions. A dean's letter plus a contract with the employer opens the door.

choices.then: Rejected: wrong form, wrong address.
No work, no risk.

title: Russian language, history and law exam
text: The exam has three modules: Russian language, history of Russia, and the basics of legislation. The residence-permit version takes about two and a quarter hours and costs about ₽5,300 at a university testing centre (prices differ by centre; the shorter patent version is about ₽4,900). Fail one module and you can retake just that one for half price; fail two or more and you retake everything at full price. Beware of anyone selling a "guaranteed result".

choices.t: Prepare properly and take the exam (₽5,300)
choices.then: You pass two modules and miss the third by a few points. You may retake only that module, at half price.
The certificate is checked in the official registry. It is not there. Serious trouble.

title: Temporary residence permit (RVP)
text: You have the language certificate and a ground for RVP (quota place, marriage to a citizen, or a Russian child). Income proof, clean record, medical certificate, fingerprints. The clerk says: "Decision within 6 months".

choices.then: Approved. The stamp goes into your passport; you no longer need a patent.
You can re-apply later.

title: Permanent residence permit (VNZh)
text: After at least a year on RVP you can apply for the residence permit (VNZh): a card valid for five years, renewable, with the right to live and work without a patent. You must show regular income, tax payments and a clean record. (In real life the waiting times are years; the game shortens them to months.)

choices.then: Approved. The VNZh card arrives: green, five years, enormous relief.
Not yet.

title: Russian citizenship
text: Normally citizenship takes about five years of residence on a residence permit, or three if you are married to a citizen. You apply with documents, an interview and an oath, and then you receive the passport. (The game shortens the waiting to a few months.)

choices.then: You cannot pay the ₽50,000 state duty yet.
Something about patience.

title: RVP quota application
text: Each region has a yearly quota for temporary residence permits. You must apply for a quota place, which may take months. The queue at the Migration Department (GUVM) starts at 5 a.m.

choices.then: You get a quota place. Now the RVP application can follow.
Marriage to a Russian citizen or having a Russian child opens RVP without the quota.

title: A "helper" at the MFC
text: A man in a leather jacket approaches you: "Documents, patent, registration — fast, ₽7,000, no queue."

choices.then: He moves to the next person.
He disappears with the money.

choices.t: Report him to the MFC guard
choices.then: The guard nods and takes a note. Maybe it helps.

title: Gosuslugi is down
text: The "State Services" website shows an error page. The queue at the MFC in person is 90 minutes.

choices.then: You read half a novel on your phone.
The page loads at 07:03.

title: Letter from the military enlistment office
text: An envelope arrives: "Please appear at the voenkomat." Rumours ripple through the family chat.

choices.then: Deferred because of studies. Stamp, signature, relief.
Ignoring does not remove the file — and fines add up.

title: Olympiad invitation
text: The school teacher says: "There is an olympiad in your subject. A winner gets extra points for admission."

choices.t: Prepare for three weeks and compete
choices.then: Not this year, but you learn a lot.
The chance passes.

title: Russian government scholarship quota
text: Rossotrudnichestvo offers quota places for foreign applicants: a year of preparatory language faculty, then the university programme.

choices.then: Accepted. Tuition free, dorm included.
Maybe next year.

title: Summons to the migration department
text: A letter says: "Appear at the department regarding violations." Your friend heard about people in the temporary detention centre waiting for deportation papers.

choices.then: The lawyer cuts the sentence: only a fine.
The hearing is five minutes. The decision is final.
Not appearing makes the file thicker.

title: Market raid at dawn
text: The doors of Sadovod are blocked. Officers walk between stalls: "Documents, everyone."

choices.then: You wait two hours and are released.
A neighbour points you out.

choices.t: Ask your employer to vouch for you
choices.then: The boss makes a call. A "mistake" is solved.

title: Banya invitation
text: A coworker invites you to a Saturday banya: steam, birch twigs, tea and honest advice.

choices.then: You leave pink, calm and with a recommendation for a better job.
He shrugs: "Next time."

title: −25 °C
text: The thermometer on the bank says −25. Your sneakers do not like it.

choices.then: Your feet thank you every winter step.
You get a cold and a lesson.

title: Annual hot water shutdown
text: A paper in the stairwell: no hot water for 14 days "for maintenance". It happens every summer.

choices.then: The ritual of the summer. Muscles of the arm: improved.
Pricey but pleasant.

title: Bank card blocked
text: SMS from a bank: "Transaction suspicious". You wired money to family and now the app says "contact support".

choices.then: A kind voice unblocks the card.
Queue + passport + a form. Done.

title: "Security service" calls
text: A voice claims to be from your bank, then from the police, then from the FSB: "Move your money to a safe account."

choices.then: You report the number. The spam calls continue anyway.
The account is empty by evening. Another victim in a very long list.

title: A dacha weekend
text: A friend drags you out to a dacha: tomatoes, grill, mosquitoes, a samovar.

choices.then: You come back with a bag of cucumbers and a sunburn.
Quiet metro, quiet flat.

title: KHL hockey night
text: A colleague has an extra ticket. The crowd chants, the beer is warm, the puck is fast.

choices.then: Your voice is gone, your mood is great.
You watch the second period in a café.

title: Lost phone on the metro
text: You realise your phone is not in your pocket. All documents, banking, taxi — gone.

choices.t: Ask the lost-and-found at the station
choices.then: A stranger handed it in!
Your SIM must be reissued with a passport visit.

title: Neighbour with a pie
text: The old woman from flat 12 rings the bell: "I baked too much. Come, eat."

choices.then: Tea with raspberry jam and the full history of the building.
She leaves the pie at your door anyway.

title: Rude remark in the shop
text: A customer behind you complains loudly about "people like you". The cashier looks away.

choices.then: You pay and leave. It stays with you for the day.
A few people nod. The customer mutters.

choices.t: Report it to the store manager
choices.then: The manager apologises and checks the camera.

title: A stranger helps
text: You are lost near the station, phone dead. A woman walks you to the right bus and hands you a pirozhok.

choices.then: Not every day is about problems.

title: Remittance to {home}
text: Your mother says the roof is leaking and your sister needs school books. Transfers cost a commission.

choices.then: The family is happy. Your wallet is not.
A small gesture, big gratitude.

choices.t: Explain that it is tight this month
choices.then: She says she understands. You hear her sigh.

title: A cousin wants to come
text: A relative asks if he can stay a week "until work starts".

choices.then: Three people in the room. Rent split, spirits up.
He finds another place — your phone stays silent for a while.

title: Mum calls
text: She asks if you eat enough, if you wear a hat and when you will visit.

choices.then: You mean it, mostly.
She says "of course" in a way that tells you otherwise.

title: Wages are late (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: Payday for the Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) job comes and goes. The boss says the money "will come on Monday".

choices.then: The money arrives on Thursday, with an apology.

choices.t: Threaten to complain to the labour inspectorate
choices.then: Fired on the spot.
You walk out with an empty envelope.

title: Unpaid overtime (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: Three hours before closing time, the manager at the Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) job says: "Everybody stays tonight".

choices.then: You stay. The boss notices.
You get half-rate for the extra hours.
The manager nods. You go home.

title: A workplace injury (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: You slip while working as Delivery courier (Yandex Eda). Your wrist hurts, and so does your pride.

choices.then: The pain grows by evening.
Without insurance the visit costs ₽3,000.

choices.t: Take the boss's cash to stay quiet
choices.then: ₽5,000 and no report. You feel uneasy.

title: Inspection at work (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: Officers with folders walk into the Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) workplace: "Inspection of labour and migration documents."

choices.then: Everything is fine. The boss pats your shoulder.
They leave without noticing you.

choices.t: Ask the boss to speak for you
choices.then: The boss says he has never seen you.

title: A promotion offer (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: The manager at the Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) job wants you for a more responsible position.

choices.then: More money, more problems.
"Forget it." The offer is withdrawn.
Fewer responsibilities, steady life.

title: Conflict with a colleague (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: A colleague at the Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) job keeps leaving you the worst tasks and makes jokes about your accent.

choices.then: You grit your teeth.
It gets worse.
The manager shrugs: "solve it yourselves".

title: A customer complains (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: A customer yells that your service is terrible. Others in line stare.

choices.then: She calms down and leaves a tip.
A complaint goes to the manager.
The manager arrives; you are excused.

title: Work without a contract (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: The boss of your Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) job: "I can pay 20% more if we skip the contract and taxes."

choices.then: The boss vanishes with two months of wages.
He finds someone else. You are out.

title: Learn a skill (Delivery courier (Yandex Eda))
text: An older colleague at the Delivery courier (Yandex Eda) job offers to show you a trick of the trade.

choices.then: You learn something that will outlast the job.
He shrugs. You do not.

title: Your home passport is expiring
text: The embassy of your country in Moscow has a long queue and strict rules. A valid national passport is needed for registration, patent and every later step.

choices.t: Renew at the embassy (₽8,000 with fees)
choices.then: New passport in six weeks. Documents stay in order.
The expiry date does not move.

title: Register with your consulate
text: Your country's consulate asks citizens abroad to register. It helps if you lose documents or need an emergency passport.

choices.then: A small card goes into your wallet. It feels reassuring.
You skip it. Famous last words.

title: Check your entry ban status
text: A friend says a violation can put you on a list that bans entry for years. You can check your status through official channels.

choices.t: Check status at the migration service
choices.then: Clean status. You exhale.
Not knowing is not safer.

title: Lost passport
text: Your wallet and passport are gone. Without it you cannot prove status, register, or work.

choices.t: Report to police and go to the embassy
choices.then: Report, embassy form, new passport in three weeks. The delay costs you.
You retrace your route. Nothing.

title: Flight home
text: A close relative is getting married at home. You can fly out for two weeks. Returning means passing border control again; any violation on your record becomes a risk.

choices.then: The wedding is loud, warm and sleepless. Return entry is smooth.
You watch the wedding on a video call.

title: A death in the family
text: Your grandfather has passed away. The family asks you to come home.

choices.then: You stand with the family. The return trip costs money and time.
The guilt walks with you for weeks.

title: Employer must notify authorities
text: Your employer must notify the migration service about hiring you. A careless employer forgets; a fair one files in three days.

choices.then: Notification sent. Papers in order.
Nothing happens. For now.

title: RVP outside quota (marriage)
text: Marriage to a Russian citizen gives you the right to apply for temporary residence without the quota. The ZAGS certificate, your partner's passport and a joint photo list are needed.

choices.then: Accepted for review. The ground for RVP is confirmed.

title: RVP outside quota (Russian child)
text: Having a child who is a Russian citizen gives you a ground for RVP without the quota.

choices.then: The migration office accepts the application as a family ground.

title: You no longer need a patent
text: The patent offices send you a farewell leaflet. RVP lets you work without it. One small paper gone.

choices.then: It tastes better than any patent receipt.

title: Residence notification
text: Residents on RVP must notify the migration service about their address and job every year.

choices.then: Done in one visit. A small win.
Forgetting costs fines later.

title: Language and history refresh
text: The citizenship interview includes questions about Russian history, law and daily life. A colleague offers to quiz you.

choices.then: You learn why Pushkin is in every textbook.
You hope for good luck.

choices.then: Coat, boots, hat. You can finally walk outside.

title: A Russian SIM card
text: Your mobile plan needs a Russian number with an identity check. Operators ask for passport and sometimes registration.

choices.t: Buy a SIM at the operator shop
choices.then: The seller asks for a SNILS number, a Gosuslugi account and biometric identification. You are told to complete the identification first (Online services → Mobile identification).
Cheap but risky; the number is blocked within a week.

title: Transport card
text: A Troika (or city) transport card comes with a small refundable deposit and makes metro, bus and tram trips cheaper than single tickets.

choices.then: Beep: you are a Moscow commuter.
It works, but costs more.

title: Pharmacy
text: You need medicine for a persistent cough. The pharmacist offers three brands and strong opinions.

choices.then: It works slowly.
It works fast.

title: Pyaterochka vs. Magnit vs. VkusVill
text: You compare prices on buckwheat, kefir and bread. A babushka beside you argues with the cashier about a ₽3 mistake.

choices.then: You walk further, save ₽400.
Convenient and costly.

title: Barbershop
text: A shop on the corner offers ₽600 haircuts with tea.

choices.then: You look like a new person.
You keep your wild hair.

title: Parcel at the pick-up point

choices.then: The clerk finds it manually.
Another trip.

title: Someone interesting
text: At a friend's tea party, a person asks you where you are from and keeps laughing at your jokes.

choices.then: You and Anna exchange numbers and a long look.
You enjoy the conversation and walk home alone.

title: A date
text: You and your partner pick a place: cafe, park, cinema, or a walk by the river.

choices.then: Candles, blini, laughter.
Autumn leaves or snow. You hold hands.
The silence on the phone says it all.

title: A quarrel
text: Money, in-laws, who forgot to buy bread: the quarrel starts small.

choices.then: It ends with tea and laughter.
The flat is very quiet.

title: Meeting the family
text: Your partner invites you to dinner with their family. Mother brings out all of the pies.

choices.then: They are polite and cold.
The door remains closed.

title: Propose?
text: You have been together for months. A ring costs ₽30,000 or a promise.

choices.then: "Not yet." The silence stretches.
Not yet.

title: ZAGS wedding
text: The civil registry office wants an application a month in advance. A small ceremony costs ₽15,000; a big one with toastmaster ₽250,000.

choices.then: The registrar stamps the certificate. You are married.
The relationship goes on.

title: News: a baby is coming
text: Two lines on the test. Joy, fear, and a hundred questions about leave, money and papers.

choices.then: You start counting the weeks and the roubles.
You talk about timing and keep going.

title: Birth at the maternity hospital
text: Contractions at 3 a.m., a taxi, a roddom (maternity ward), and a tiny cry at sunrise.

choices.then: A healthy baby! You collect the paperwork for the birth certificate and the child's status.

title: What to do with maternity capital
text: Your maternity capital certificate sits in the app. A neighbour who has a mortgage tells you it can go towards a down payment, to repair or build a home, to pay for education, or to a mother's pension. It cannot simply be taken out as cash.

choices.t: Plan to use it for a home (Real estate agency)
choices.then: You note it down: the agency can apply it to a purchase.

choices.t: Read the rules for education and pension use
choices.then: The options are many; the paperwork is longer than you hoped.

title: Newborn paperwork
text: Birth certificate at ZAGS, child registration, SNILS and a polyclinic attachment.

choices.t: Do it all in one trip
choices.then: Done. You celebrate with a pastry.

title: Kindergarten queue
text: Gosuslugi says you are 214th in the queue for a place. Private kindergartens ask ₽45,000 a month.

choices.then: You find a nanny meanwhile.
Expensive, but the child is happy.

title: Child has a fever
text: The thermometer says 38.9 at 2 a.m. The pediatrician hotline plays a recording.

choices.then: Doctors arrive, calm everyone. Not serious.
Raspberries, tea, a long night.

title: Child's birthday
text: Balloons, cake, a clown who has seen better days.

choices.then: Twenty kids and a broken vase.
Quieter and sweeter.

title: Marriage on the rocks
text: You and your partner have not said a kind word in weeks.

choices.then: An awkward hour, a first honest talk.
ZAGS stamp, one hour. A lighter wallet and heavier heart.

title: Your partner's papers
text: Your partner's registration is expiring, and the work patent is not renewed. The couple's conversations start sounding like migration forms.

choices.then: You spend the weekend with the MFC and a thermos.
They notice.

title: Making a friend
text: A neighbour from the stairwell asks if you want to go to the banya, play football or just talk.

choices.then: Phone numbers, tea and a friend.
Friendship waits.

The plan stays on your list.

title: Yekaterinburg's Europe–Asia obelisk: take photos at the best light
text: Early or late, the light is magical. The place: Yekaterinburg's Europe–Asia obelisk — a conventional marker on the border between two continents.

choices.t: Take photos at the best light
choices.then: You photograph Yekaterinburg's Europe–Asia obelisk in perfect light. People ask where it is.
The plan stays on your list.

title: Yekaterinburg's Europe–Asia obelisk: read about its history
text: Spend an hour with a book or a museum panel. The place: Yekaterinburg's Europe–Asia obelisk — a conventional marker on the border between two continents.

choices.then: You learn why Yekaterinburg's Europe–Asia obelisk matters: a conventional marker on the border between two continents.
The plan stays on your list.

title: Nominated for the community «Patriot» Award
text: Neighbours, teachers and volunteers have nominated you. The National «Patriot» Award is a public award for those who do not stand aside: people and organisations who develop and improve everyday life in Russia — through culture, knowledge, volunteering and care for their neighbours. A small ceremony is held at the community centre.

choices.then: You are applauded by people whose names you now know. A certificate, a medal and a pot of tea.

choices.t: Decline modestly and credit the whole community
choices.then: Your humility makes the audience clap even louder. The award is given on behalf of the whole courtyard.

title: A word from the community centre
text: The coordinator says: "People notice what you do. Keep learning, keep helping — recognition follows." (Community merit: 15–39.)

choices.then: You feel useful and a little proud.

title: Everyday life: Tea culture
text: A colleague pours tea from a samovar and offers jam instead of sugar. (Russians often take tea with jam, lemon or sweets, and an invitation for "a cup of tea" can last for hours.)

choices.then: You learn three recipes for pirozhki and one family secret.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Shoes at the door
text: A friend hands you slippers (tapochki) at the door. (Taking off your shoes in the hall is standard in Russian homes; guests usually get slippers.)

choices.t: Say thank you and change shoes
choices.then: Your friend smiles; you have passed a small test of manners.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Flowers and odd numbers
text: You are invited to a birthday dinner. (Flowers are given in odd numbers for celebrations; even numbers are for funerals.)

choices.then: The hostess places them in a vase with pride.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Dacha season
text: A colleague invites you to help prepare the dacha for the season. (Millions of families grow vegetables and spend weekends at their dacha.)

choices.then: Your hands are blistered; the sunset is worth it.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Banya etiquette
text: A neighbour takes you to a traditional banya. (The banya is a steam bath with birch twigs (veniki) and tea; it is a social ritual.)

choices.then: You emerge pink and philosophical.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Hospitality
text: A family you barely know invites you for dinner "just to meet". (Russian hospitality can mean more food than anyone can eat. Refusing a second plate is almost impossible.)

choices.then: You stagger home with a bag of leftovers.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Polite forms
text: You hear "ты" and "вы" in the same conversation. (Russian has formal "вы" and informal "ты"; the switch is a small social milestone.)

choices.then: Your friend finally says "let's switch to ты". You feel promoted.
You move on.

title: Everyday life: Metro as architecture
text: You ride the Moscow metro on a quiet afternoon. (Many Moscow stations — Komsomolskaya, Mayakovskaya, Novoslobodskaya — look like palaces and are cultural attractions.)

choices.then: You exit three stations later with a camera full of mosaics.
You move on.

title: Electronics mall: phones
text: Rows of glass cases, a salesperson in a branded T-shirt and a tag that says "0% instalment". Your current phone is battery-hungry and the screen is cracked.

choices.then: The salesperson hands you three boxes.

choices.t: Check used phones on the classifieds board
choices.then: A notice board full of numbers, photos and "urgent, moving abroad".
You admire the flagship and leave.

title: Cracked screen
text: You drop your phone on the tram floor. The glass spiderwebs.

choices.then: The repair stall in the passage fixes it in an hour.
The cracks cut your finger twice a day.

title: Driving school
text: A banner says: "Licence in two months, 100% pass rate". A course costs about ₽35,000 in the game (real prices are often ₽30,000 to ₽80,000) and includes theory lessons, practical driving lessons (the national programme changed in March 2026) and an exam at the traffic police: first theory, then practical driving.

choices.then: You sign the contract. First theory class on Monday.
You take a leaflet and a lollipop.

title: Your licence from home
text: You have a valid driving licence from your home country. A friend says that a foreigner with a valid licence can get a Russian one by passing only the theory exam at the traffic police, with a medical certificate, instead of a full driving school (a simplified summary; check the current rules).

choices.t: Prepare and sit the theory exam (₽5,500 with the medical certificate)
choices.then: You miss the pass mark on the theory test. You may try again.
You put the licence in your wallet and move on.

title: Traffic police exam
text: Theory test on a touch screen, then the practical exam on a closed track and in town.

choices.then: You pass. A plastic card with your photo and a very large smile.
You promise to revise more.

title: Car dealership
text: Polished floors, a smell of new plastic and a sales manager with a smile: "What are you looking for — comfort, economy, status?" Prices are in the millions, used cars are cheaper.

choices.then: The manager leads you outside past rows of hatchbacks.

choices.t: Look at new cars on credit
choices.then: He opens a folder of leasing offers.
You take a spin around the block. Heated seats are a revelation.
You promise to come back.

title: Traffic police stop
text: A patrol officer waves a striped baton: "Documents, please."

choices.then: Everything is in order. He salutes.

choices.t: Politely ask for his name and reason
choices.then: He hands the documents back after a short silence.

title: Parking fine
text: A parking inspector sticks a ticket on your windscreen.

choices.then: Paid in the Gosuslugi app within five days.
The fine doubles later.

title: Dead battery
text: It is −18 °C and your car does not start.

choices.t: Ask a neighbour for a jump start
choices.then: A man in felt boots helps you. Everyone has done this.
Quick, expensive.

title: Winter tyres
text: The first snow is falling and your tyres are bald.

choices.then: You drive safely all winter.
You slide into a snowbank.

title: Car sharing / taxi side job
text: A friend says you can earn money driving at weekends.

choices.t: Try a weekend of taxi rides
choices.then: You earn ₽6,000 and learn every pothole.
Quiet weekends.

title: Hitchhiker in the snow
text: A woman with groceries waves at the road in a blizzard.

choices.then: She gives you a jar of pickles and her life story.
You feel guilty for two kilometres.

title: Minor accident
text: A scratch and a dent: another driver reversed into you.

choices.then: Ten minutes of forms, no police needed.
You wait two hours in the cold.

title: Insurance renewal
text: The OSAGO policy expires next week.

choices.then: Quick and cheap with a no-accident discount.
A fine awaits.

title: Real estate agency
text: Brochures of towers and cottages, a coffee machine and an agent called Elvira. "Rent, buy, mortgage — what is your dream?"

choices.then: She opens the rental catalogue.
She slides a folder of properties across the desk.

choices.t: Ask about registration and rental contracts
choices.then: She explains how to protect yourself from fake landlords.
You promise to call.

title: Too good to be true
text: An online ad: a flat in the centre for half the market price. "Send the deposit today, I am abroad."

choices.then: You report the ad.
The ad disappears. So does the money.

title: A relative is in hospital
text: Your partner calls: a close family member was admitted overnight. Visiting hours are 17:00–19:00, and no flowers on the ward.

choices.t: Visit after work with soup and juice
choices.then: You sit by the bed and listen. They squeeze your hand.
A nurse is always at the bedside. It helps the family sleep.

choices.t: Send a message and stay at work
choices.then: The silence on the phone is heavy.

title: Blood donor desk
text: A banner in the corridor: "Every donation can save up to three lives."

choices.then: You feel dizzy and proud; a nurse gives you tea and chocolate.
You promise to come back.

title: First aid on the metro
text: A man collapses on the platform. People stand around with phones. Someone shouts "Does anyone know first aid?"

choices.then: You do what you can: call 103 and keep him warm. The medics praise you.
You call for help and keep the crowd back.

title: You give an injection
text: A frightened patient on the ward needs an intramuscular injection. Their hands are shaking; so are yours.

choices.t: Check the name and dose, then do it calmly
choices.then: The patient flinches and a bruise forms. You apologise and keep calm.

choices.t: Ask a senior nurse to supervise
choices.then: She nods approvingly and you learn the trick of the angle.

title: A stray dog in the courtyard
text: A thin dog with matted fur watches you from behind a bin. It shivers. Snow is falling.

choices.then: The dog wolfs the sausage and follows you to the door, then stops.
A volunteer takes the details and promises to come in the evening.
The vet cleans it, vaccinates it and says: "Healthy and very sweet." Now it needs a home.
The dog watches you leave. You feel its eyes in your back.

title: A pack of stray dogs
text: Three big dogs trot along the road at dusk. One of them growls.

choices.t: Stand still, avoid eye contact and back away slowly
choices.then: The pack loses interest. Your heart beats for a minute.

choices.t: Take another route and report to the city animal service
choices.then: You walk longer but feel safer.

choices.t: Throw a stone to scare them
choices.then: One barks and snaps. You run and fall in the snow.

title: A found dog with a collar
text: A friendly spaniel with a tag on its collar and nobody around. It looks lost, not abandoned.

choices.t: Post a "found" ad in the neighbourhood chat
choices.then: Within two hours a tearful owner calls. "Thank you, thank you!"

choices.t: Take it to a vet to read the chip
choices.then: The vet scans the chip and calls the owner. A happy reunion.
Someone else will help.

choices.then: Tents, campfire and a sky with too many stars.
You hear about the mosquitos afterwards.

title: Embroidery circle
text: The grandmothers of the neighbourhood meet to knit, embroider and gossip.

choices.then: Your first row is crooked, your first scarf is long. They adopt you.
You get a plate of pirozhki and a seat.

title: Photo walk
text: Photographers meet to walk through old courtyards at golden hour.

choices.then: You find a doorway that looks like a painting.
You take forty photos of one lamp post.

title: Amateur theatre
text: The community drama club needs actors for a village play.

choices.then: You get the role of the third peasant. You are brilliant.
You paint a tree for six hours and love it.

title: Friday prayer and a shared lunch
text: A mosque in the city invites the neighbourhood for a community lunch after the prayer.

choices.then: Plov, flatbread and tea. The imam asks about your family.
The smell of food follows you home.

title: An Orthodox liturgy
text: The church bells ring on a Sunday morning. Candles flicker, a choir sings.

choices.then: The singing carries you away. Nobody minds that you are only watching.
A kind old woman gives you a rusk and a smile.

title: A Buddhist datsan
text: In a Buddhist temple, monks chant, prayer wheels spin and visitors walk clockwise.

choices.t: Visit respectfully and turn the wheels
choices.then: A monk shows you how to spin them. You leave calm.
A sign asks politely not to.

title: Shabbat dinner
text: A Jewish community invites guests for a Friday night dinner.

choices.then: Candles, bread, songs, jokes. You are asked a hundred questions.
They promise a plate for next time.

title: Iftar during Ramadan
text: A neighbour from Dagestan invites you to break the fast at sunset.

choices.then: Dates, soup, bread and a long conversation about patience.
It is gratefully accepted.

title: Epiphany ice-hole swim
text: On 19 January many Orthodox believers dip in an ice hole cut in a river or lake.

choices.t: Watch with a flask of tea
choices.then: Steam rises from brave swimmers. You applaud.
Three seconds of terror, three hours of glow.

title: Christmas carols
text: Children go from door to door singing carols for sweets.

choices.t: Open the door and give sweets
choices.then: They sing off-key and sweetly.
Disappointed voices drift away.

title: Apple Spas
text: On 19 August Orthodox communities bless the first apples of the season.

choices.t: Take a bag of apples to be blessed
choices.then: Everyone shares them afterwards.
Crisp, sweet and cheap.

title: Flu shot
text: The polyclinic offers a free flu vaccination in autumn.

choices.then: A small pinch and a sticker: "I was brave."
You catch the flu in November.

title: Birch pollen allergy
text: Birches bloom and your nose runs like a tap.

choices.then: You can breathe, mostly.
Two weeks of sneezing.

title: A tick bite
text: After a walk in the forest you find a tick on your leg.

choices.t: Go to the emergency room to remove it
choices.then: They remove it and advise about the vaccine.
You manage, with trembling hands.

title: Heat wave
text: Thirty-five degrees in the shade and no air conditioning.

choices.then: You survive with a wet towel and a book.
Dizziness, headache and a very long nap.

title: Sleepless nights
text: You cannot sleep. The white nights, the stress and the noise do not help.

choices.t: Set a routine and cut screens
choices.then: It works, slowly.
You are a zombie all day.

title: Back pain
text: Lifting boxes has left you with a sore back.

choices.then: Exercises, heat and advice. It helps.
The pain returns after a day.

title: A first-aid course
text: A free first-aid course is offered at the community centre.

choices.then: You learn CPR on a dummy named Vasya.
You hope you never need it.

title: Dentist
text: A tooth hurts when you drink something cold.

choices.then: A small filling and a lecture about flossing.
The tooth becomes a major project later.

title: Winter vitamin D
text: The sun disappears in November and you feel gloomy and tired.

choices.t: Take vitamin D and walk in daylight
choices.then: By January you feel human.
The grey season feels longer.

title: Counselling hotline
text: A free psychological hotline works day and night.

choices.t: Call and talk for half an hour
choices.then: The voice is kind. You feel lighter.

choices.t: Write a letter you do not send
choices.then: Even that helps a little.

title: Quit smoking
text: A friend dares you to stop smoking for a month.

choices.then: The first week is hell; the third week is wonderful.
You promise to start on Monday.

title: A sports injury
text: You twist your ankle on the ice.

choices.then: X-ray, bandage, crutches and a medical note.
It gets worse before it gets better.

title: The lift is stuck
text: The lift stops between floors and the emergency button hums.

choices.t: Press the call button and wait
choices.then: A technician arrives in thirty minutes. A neighbour offers sweets to keep your spirits up.

choices.t: Call a neighbour on your phone
choices.then: He laughs: "I am in the same lift!"

title: Noisy repairs
text: Neighbours are drilling at 7 a.m. on Saturday. Quiet hours are officially from 23:00 to 7:00.

choices.t: Knock politely and ask for a break
choices.then: They apologise and finish by noon.
The drilling gets louder.

title: The heating season
text: The radiators are still cold even though it is below zero.

choices.then: They promise to switch it on "this week". It is on in two days.
Warm but expensive.

title: Babushkas on the bench
text: The grandmothers on the bench ask where you are going, who with and whether you have eaten.

choices.t: Stop and chat for five minutes
choices.then: You get a recipe, a warning about the weather and a blessing.

choices.t: Say good morning and walk on
choices.then: They mutter approvingly.

title: Stray cats in the basement
text: Cats live in your building's basement. A neighbour feeds them every day.

choices.then: A fluffy ginger cat purrs against your leg.
The ginger cat judges you.

title: Courtyard football
text: Boys in the courtyard are playing football and ask if you want to join.

choices.then: You are the goalkeeper and the worst defender.
You applaud a spectacular own goal.

title: Waste sorting initiative
text: A group wants to start waste sorting in the courtyard.

choices.then: Containers appear. The neighbours are proud.
You cheer them on.

title: A pothole petition
text: Residents are signing a petition about a dangerous pothole near the school.

choices.then: It is fixed within a month. You feel powerful.
It remains a local landmark.

title: A new neighbour
text: A family moves in across the landing with boxes, a cat and a loud toddler.

choices.t: Bring bread and salt as a welcome
choices.then: It is a custom for new homes: bread for abundance, salt for good luck.
A polite nod.

title: Snowman contest
text: The management company holds a snowman contest in the courtyard.

choices.t: Build a snowman with the kids
choices.then: Yours has a carrot nose and a scarf. It wins "the most original".

choices.t: Judge the entries from the window
choices.then: You applaud with mittens on.

title: The dvornik
text: The caretaker asks you to move your bike so he can clear the snow.

choices.then: He grins: "A good tenant."
He moves it himself, muttering.

title: A lost parcel
text: A courier left your parcel with a neighbour you have never met.

choices.t: Knock on every door to find it
choices.then: It takes twenty minutes and three cups of tea. You find it in flat 33.
Quick, but expensive.

title: Your birthday
text: It is your birthday. Friends ask where the party is.

choices.t: Throw a small party at home
choices.then: Salad, pies and loud laughter. A neighbour knocks at midnight, then joins.
Tea, a call from home and a slice of cake.

title: A friend's wedding
text: You are invited as a guest to a big wedding with a toastmaster and a hundred guests.

choices.t: Go and give a gift envelope (₽5,000)
choices.then: Toasts, dancing and a long table. You cry at the vows.
A warm message and a promise to meet soon.

title: A housewarming
text: A friend has moved to a new flat and invites you for a housewarming party.

choices.t: Bring bread, salt and a plant
choices.then: The host says: "Wealth to this house."
Warm but simple.

title: A funeral of a neighbour
text: An elderly neighbour has died. The building gathers to pay respects.

choices.then: You carry chairs, pour tea and stand silently. The family thanks you.
A short message. It is received with gratitude.

title: First salary
text: The money lands on your card for the first time: a small, real sum.

choices.t: Treat yourself and a friend to dinner
choices.then: You pay the bill with a grin.
You write the number in your notebook.

title: A breakup
text: A relationship ends with a short message and a long silence.

choices.then: You eat dumplings at midnight and cry and laugh.
It helps, until Sunday.

title: A school reunion
text: Your old classmates organise a reunion in a café.

choices.then: Everyone has changed; nothing has.
You prefer the memory.

title: A promotion party
text: A colleague has been promoted and brings a cake to the office.

choices.then: He remembers it later when he needs a favour.
The cake is delicious anyway.

title: A retirement
text: A senior colleague is retiring after forty years and the whole office is moved.

choices.then: Your voice trembles. People applaud.
A small message, a big signature.

title: Moving day
text: You need to move to a new flat and your friends offer to help for pizza.

choices.then: Boxes, tape and a fridge that does not fit through the door. You laugh through it.
Efficient and silent.

title: An anniversary
text: You have been together for a year. A restaurant or a long walk?

choices.then: Candles, wine and a small gift.

choices.t: A long walk and a thermos of tea
choices.then: Simple, warm and perfect.

title: A lottery ticket
text: A neighbour presses a lottery ticket into your hand: "For luck."

choices.then: You win ₽100. You buy another one.
He shrugs: "Your loss."

title: A lost wallet is returned
text: A stranger calls: "I found your wallet. Meet me at the metro."

choices.t: Meet and thank him with a reward
choices.then: Everything is inside. He refuses the reward; you buy him a coffee.
He agrees, but it takes a week.

title: You are laid off
text: The manager invites you to his office and offers you tea, which is never a good sign.

choices.then: You get two weeks' pay and a letter of recommendation.
You leave with nothing and a sore pride.

title: The 11.11 sale
text: Every marketplace screams "Mega sale!" and your phone buzzes constantly.

choices.then: You save 20% on winter boots.
Your wallet weeps.

title: A late salary
text: Payday passes and the money has not arrived. The accountant says "Friday".

choices.then: It arrives on Thursday evening.
The accountant is annoyed but pays on the same day.

title: A pay-raise conversation
text: You think you deserve a raise. The manager is in a good mood after lunch.

choices.t: Ask, with examples of your results
choices.then: He grumbles and agrees to a small raise.
Nobody notices.

title: Bank deposit
text: The bank sells you a deposit with a bright pamphlet. The rate looks high.

choices.t: Read the terms and choose carefully
choices.then: You find a fair one with a safe insurance limit.
The conditions have a catch.

title: A friend asks for a loan
text: A friend asks for ₽5,000 until payday.

choices.then: He repays on time and buys you a coffee.
He understands, mostly.

title: Crowdfunding for a friend
text: A message circulates: a friend's child needs treatment and the family is collecting donations.

choices.then: You are thanked by the whole family.
The message reaches ten more people.

title: Tipping etiquette
text: The waiter was excellent. In Russia tipping is about 5–10%.

choices.then: The waiter beams and brings candy.
He shrugs; you feel a bit mean.

title: Bargaining at a bazaar
text: A seller at a bazaar names a high price with a charming smile.

choices.then: You win ₽300 off and a gift of dried apricots.
He smiles even wider.

title: Flea market
text: A Saturday flea market offers samovars, records and mysterious cameras.

choices.then: A 1970s camera that actually works.
You find three things you do not need and buy none.

title: Loyalty cards
text: The cashier asks: "Do you have our card?" and a queue holds its breath.

choices.then: The cashier sighs with theatrical patience.
Points, coupons and a pile of notifications.

title: A utility subsidy
text: You hear that families with low income can apply for a housing subsidy.

choices.then: A month later your bills are lower.
Your bills stay high.

title: Pension info
text: A relative asks about the pension fund. You read up on how contributions work.

choices.then: You learn a lot and make a plan.
There is time.

title: First snow
text: You wake up to a white world: roofs, trees, benches, all covered.

choices.then: Squeaky snow under your boots and a quiet city.
The window is a postcard.

title: Spring thaw
text: The snow turns to puddles and the pavement to a river.

choices.then: You keep your feet dry and your spirits high.
Soaked within a block.

title: Birch sap
text: Villagers sell fresh birch sap in plastic bottles by the road.

choices.then: Sweet, clear and strange. A taste of spring.
Next year.

title: A mayovka picnic
text: In May, people grill shashlik in parks and forests; the smell is everywhere.

choices.then: Meat, tea and music from a phone. You come back sunburnt.
The neighbours smell it and say nothing.

title: Swimming in the lake
text: On a hot day the lake near the city fills with swimmers.

choices.then: Cold, then delicious.
A cold drink and a new tan line.

title: Thunderstorm
text: A summer thunderstorm rolls over the city; the power flickers.

choices.t: Light candles and watch the storm
choices.then: A small blackout feels like a gift.
Roads flooded but you are fine.

title: Golden autumn
text: The leaves turn gold and every park is a postcard.

choices.t: Walk in a park with a thermos
choices.then: You collect maple leaves and a good mood.
The golden light comes through the curtains anyway.

title: A New Year market
text: Christmas markets pop up with wooden huts, mulled wine and handmade crafts.

choices.then: You find a hand-painted ornament and a warm scarf.
The lights are enough.

title: Buying the New Year tree
text: The tree market is full of pine and spruce trees and tinsel.

choices.then: Your flat smells like a forest for two weeks.
It is easier, if less magical.

title: Decorating the courtyard
text: Neighbours put lights and a tree in the courtyard for New Year.

choices.then: Hot tea afterwards and a courtyard that glows.
You enjoy the glow with a warm cup.

title: Old New Year
text: On the night of 13–14 January some families celebrate the Old New Year.

choices.then: A second New Year with the same salad. Nobody minds.
You wake up refreshed.

title: A snowstorm day
text: A blizzard shuts the city for a day. Schools are closed and the roads are empty.

choices.t: Stay home with tea and a good book
choices.then: You treat it like a holiday.
You make the first tracks in the new snow.

title: The white nights
text: In the northern city it does not get dark until almost dawn.

choices.t: Walk along the river at midnight
choices.then: Pink light on the water. Nobody sleeps.
Sleep wins.

title: Harvest at the dacha
text: A colleague's dacha is overflowing with tomatoes and cucumbers.

choices.then: You return with three bags and a recipe for pickles.
Pale tomatoes, high prices.

title: Back-to-school stationery
text: Stationery shops are full of notebooks, pens and bright backpacks.

choices.t: Buy a good notebook and a pen
choices.then: A fresh notebook feels like a new life.
It works.

title: Tatiana's Day (Students' Day)
text: Students celebrate the patron saint of their university. Songs, silly costumes and a very relaxed attitude to timetables.

choices.then: You dance in a circle and sing the university anthem off-key.
Exams wait for no one.

choices.t: Call a friend from the old university
choices.then: You swap stories for an hour.

title: Valentine's Day
text: Shops fill with pink hearts and flowers. Some say it is imported, but everyone buys the chocolates.

choices.t: Buy a small gift for someone
choices.then: A card and a chocolate heart. A smile.
Pizza and a bad romantic comedy.
It is just a Tuesday.

title: World Theatre Day
text: Theatres across the country offer free open rehearsals and backstage tours.

choices.then: You watch a scene repeated eleven times and fall in love with the craft.
You see a classic from the balcony with a hundred students.
The theatre will be there next year.

title: Cosmonautics Day
text: On 12 April Russia celebrates Yuri Gagarin's first spaceflight in 1961. Museums, planetariums and space-themed concerts fill the city.

choices.then: Rockets, capsules and the smell of old metal. You leave feeling small and inspired.

choices.t: Look at the stars from a roof
choices.then: A friend brings a telescope. Jupiter looks like a pearl.
Tubes of puree, as in the old days. Strangely good.

title: Spring and Labour Day
text: The first of May: a day off, banners, picnics and the opening of the dacha season.

choices.t: Go to a dacha with friends
choices.then: Shashlik, mud and a lot of laughter.
A concert, balloons and sticky candy floss.
Holiday pay, but a tired Friday.

title: Day of Slavic Writing and Culture
text: On 24 May the country honours Saints Cyril and Methodius and the alphabet that carries their names.

choices.t: Attend a reading in the library
choices.then: You hear poems in Old Church Slavonic and modern Russian side by side.
You practise a beautiful cursive and send it to a friend.

choices.t: Visit a monument to Cyril and Methodius
choices.then: A quiet moment in a busy city.

title: Children's Day
text: Playgrounds fill with face painting, balloons and giant bubbles.

choices.then: You paint faces for four hours. A fox, a tiger, a very serious Spider-Man.

choices.t: Take your own child out for ice cream
choices.then: Chocolate on the nose and sunshine.
A quiet afternoon.

title: Pushkin Day and Russian Language Day
text: On 6 June, Pushkin's birthday, people read his verses in parks, schools and metro stations.

choices.then: You stumble over the meter and the audience applauds the effort.

choices.t: Listen to a reading at a monument
choices.then: A grandmother recites "I remember a wondrous moment" from memory.
Today's word: "umilenie" (tender emotion). You use it three times.

title: Day of Family, Love and Fidelity
text: On 8 July people give chamomile flowers and celebrate Saints Peter and Fevronia, the patrons of marriage.

choices.t: Spend the day with your loved ones
choices.then: A picnic, chamomile flowers and a promise for another year.
You talk for two hours and cry a little.

choices.t: Do volunteering at a children's home
choices.then: A day you will remember.

title: The Transfiguration (Apple Spas)
text: On 19 August Orthodox communities bless the first fruits of the harvest.

choices.t: Take apples to be blessed and share them
choices.then: Everyone shares and the church smells of apples and incense.
Crisp and sweet.
The flat smells like autumn.

title: Teachers' Day
text: Students bring flowers to school and thank their teachers. Even adults remember the one teacher who changed their lives.

choices.then: The reply arrives in an hour: three lines and a lot of emotion.

choices.t: Bring flowers to a teacher at your school or university
choices.then: She says "you did not have to" and then glows.
You think about it on the bus.

title: Constitution Day
text: A day off for many, with ceremonies and a discussion about the rights and duties written in the constitution.

choices.then: It is shorter than you thought, and longer than you read.

choices.t: Use the day off for errands
choices.then: The banks are closed; the shops are open.
A rare quiet day.

title: A colleague asks about Tajik poetry
text: A colleague saw a statue and asks who Rudaki is. You know the answer: a 10th-century poet honoured as a founder of Persian poetry, with a monument in Dushanbe.

choices.t: Recite a few lines and explain
choices.then: She listens as if to music. "Say it again, slowly."

choices.t: Say it is hard to translate
choices.then: She nods and writes the name down to look it up later.

title: Cook qurutob for friends
text: You miss qurutob, the national dish of flatbread, dried yoghurt balls (qurut) and vegetables served on one big dish.

choices.then: They eat with their hands, as you show them. The dish disappears in ten minutes.
It tastes of home, and of distance.

title: A concert of Shashmaqom
text: A cultural centre announces an evening of Shashmaqom, the classical music tradition of Central Asia shared by Tajiks and Uzbeks.

choices.then: The long, slow melodies surprise them. "It is like jazz that has lived for centuries," one says.

choices.t: Listen to a recording at home
choices.then: You close your eyes and are in your grandmother's courtyard.

title: The mountains in your memory
text: A friend shows photos of the Alps. You think of the Pamir: Ismoil Somoni Peak, 7,495 metres, the highest point of Tajikistan.

choices.then: Peaks, glacier lakes and a bus on a cliff road. The friend goes quiet: "I want to go."
You keep your mountains to yourself for now.

title: A postcard of Iskanderkul
text: Your mother sends a photo of Iskanderkul, the turquoise lake in the Fann Mountains, with the words "Come home for a summer".

choices.then: You make a plan on the back of an envelope. It feels good to have one.

choices.t: Reply with a heart and a joke
choices.then: You cannot promise anything yet.

title: A teahouse in Moscow
text: You find a Central Asian teahouse (choyxona) with low tables, green tea and carpets on the walls.

choices.t: Sit for an hour with tea and bread
choices.then: The owner speaks your language. For one hour the city disappears.
Not today.

title: Mehrgon in the autumn
text: In autumn the Mehrgon festival celebrates the harvest. A cultural centre organises a small gathering.

choices.then: Fruit, music and old songs. A neighbour from Samarkand brings pomegranates.

choices.t: Stay in with a phone call
choices.then: Your family sends a video of the harvest.

title: Two languages in one day
text: In the morning you speak Tajik to a cousin, at work Russian to the manager, and at night a mix of both to a friend. You notice it is tiring and wonderful.

choices.t: Teach a colleague "thank you" in Tajik
choices.then: The word "rahmat" spreads through the office. Everyone says it for a week.
You listen to a podcast on the way home.

title: Why is the capital called Dushanbe?
text: A friend asks about the name of your capital. You explain that "Dushanbe" means "Monday" in Tajik, after the market that was held on Mondays.

choices.then: He laughs: "So our Monday is your city!"

choices.t: Say it is a long story
choices.then: He promises to ask again.

title: A book by Sadriddin Ayni
text: A Russian reader asks for a Central Asian novel to read. You think of Sadriddin Ayni, the founder of modern Tajik literature.

choices.t: Recommend his work and offer to translate a page
choices.then: She keeps the page folded in her bag for weeks.
She buys Tolstoy and thanks you.

title: The old fortress at Hisor
text: A documentary on TV shows the Hisor fortress near Dushanbe. Your flatmates ask if you have been.

choices.t: Describe the road and the old gate
choices.then: You tell it as a story. By the end they have booked a trip in their minds.

choices.t: Say you were there once as a child
choices.then: A smile and a quiet memory.

title: Baking sambusa for the office
text: Your birthday is next week. You could bake sambusa, pastries with meat and onion, for your colleagues.

choices.then: The tray is empty before lunch. Someone asks for the recipe, someone else for a second tray.
Easy, but no one asks for the recipe.

title: The Registan in a photograph
text: A coworker has a postcard of the Registan in Samarkand: three grand madrasahs around a square. "Have you been?" she asks.

choices.t: Tell her about the evening light
choices.then: The blue tiles turn gold. She decides to go next spring.

choices.t: Say it looks small on a postcard
choices.then: She laughs. "Then I must see it."

title: The astronomer king
text: You read a news item about stars and remember Ulugh Beg, the 15th-century ruler of Samarkand who built a great observatory.

choices.t: Share the story with a friend who loves space
choices.then: He is amazed that the star catalogue was so accurate. "Five hundred years before telescopes!"
Quiet pride.

title: Navoi on a bookshelf
text: In a library you find a book by Alisher Navoi, the great poet of the Chagatai language. The librarian asks if you know him.

choices.then: The librarian writes it down. "Beautiful," she says.

choices.t: Say you know him from school
choices.then: She nods, impressed.

title: The right way to cook plov
text: Your friends argue about plov: which rice, which meat, which pot. Only you know the real answer.

choices.t: Cook a big cauldron on Saturday
choices.then: Carrots, cumin, patience. They declare it "the best thing ever" and ask you to teach them.
They take notes and burn the rice.

title: The towers of Bukhara
text: A magazine shows the Kalyan minaret in Bukhara. You say you have walked in its shadow.

choices.t: Tell them about the old bazaar domes
choices.then: You describe the trading domes and the smell of spices. They listen like children.
You smile at the picture.

title: A suzani on the wall
text: Your mother sent a suzani, an embroidered cloth, as a gift. It brightens the flat.

choices.t: Hang it and tell visitors the story
choices.then: Everyone touches the stitches. Your flat feels warmer.
It stays in a drawer, a promise of a future home.

title: Who was Amir Timur?
text: A history debate starts at lunch about Tamerlane, known in Uzbekistan as Amir Timur. People have strong and different opinions.

choices.t: Explain how he is remembered in Uzbekistan
choices.then: You are careful and calm. The debate ends with curiosity, not heat.
A wise decision some days.

title: The mahalla spirit
text: Your neighbours here are cold, and you remember the mahalla, the close neighbourhood community at home where everyone knows everyone.

choices.t: Organise a small tea gathering on the stairs
choices.then: Four doors open. A new kind of mahalla is born.

choices.t: Keep to yourself and miss home
choices.then: It is a quiet evening.

title: Khiva on the screen
text: A travel show features Khiva, a walled city of the Silk Road whose old town Itchan Kala is a UNESCO heritage site.

choices.t: Say you have seen it and recommend the sunset
choices.then: The host says the same words on screen and you laugh.
You feel homesick all the same.

title: The metro that looks like a palace
text: You compare Moscow's palatial stations with the Tashkent metro, opened in 1977, whose stations are decorated with ceramics and carvings.

choices.t: Tell your Moscow friends and compare stations
choices.then: They are surprised: "We have not seen that!" You take photos next time at home.
The tunnel lights flash past.

title: Silk Road jokes
text: A colleague asks if your grandfather rode a camel on the Silk Road. You laugh and answer properly.

choices.t: Tell the real story of trade routes and bazaars
choices.then: The joke ends; the interest begins.
Everyone laughs, nobody learns.

title: A wedding plov
text: A friend of the family is getting married in Moscow and wants you to cook the wedding plov.

choices.t: Agree and cook for two hundred
choices.then: You wake at 4 a.m. and cook until noon. Applause follows you home.

choices.t: Offer to help instead of lead
choices.then: The big pot is in better hands, and you stir.

title: The epic of Manas
text: A friend hears that Kyrgyz people memorise an epic hero's story longer than many novels. "Is it true?" he asks.

choices.t: Explain that the Manas epic is one of the longest in the world and is performed by manaschi storytellers
choices.then: He is speechless. "And people perform it from memory?"

choices.t: Say it is a long story
choices.then: He asks you to tell some of it next time.

title: Issyk-Kul in your head
text: A photo of a lake in the mountains reminds you of Issyk-Kul, one of the largest mountain lakes in the world.

choices.t: Tell them that it does not freeze even in winter
choices.then: They are surprised, as they thought only the Baikal could surprise them.

choices.t: Show a photo from your phone
choices.then: A blue, endless sheet of water.

title: A yurt in a park
text: A festival in a Moscow park shows a yurt. The guide speaks about the "tunduk", the ring at the top of the roof.

choices.t: Add that the tunduk is on the national flag
choices.then: The guide is delighted. "Do you want to tell the next group?"
It is nice to hear it from someone else.

title: Ala-kiyiz, a felt carpet
text: You are given a traditional felt carpet, an ala-kiyiz, made by your aunt.

choices.t: Place it in the centre of your room
choices.then: Friends sit on it, take their shoes off, and relax. The room feels like a home.
Colour and craft in a grey flat.

title: Kumys on the table
text: A Kazakh friend brings kumys, the fermented mare's milk loved in Central Asia. You raise a glass with him.

choices.then: Sour, fizzy, and wonderfully familiar. You talk until midnight.
He understands and drinks it for you.

title: Kok-boru on the screen
text: On TV, horse riders fight over a goat carcass in a game called kok-boru, a traditional Central Asian sport.

choices.t: Explain the rules to your puzzled flatmates
choices.then: They are aghast and fascinated. "Is it safe?" "Very, if you can ride."
You are not in the mood.

title: Eagle hunters
text: A documentary shows berkutchi, eagle hunters of Kyrgyzstan who train golden eagles to hunt foxes.

choices.t: Tell your friends you know a family who do it
choices.then: They ask a hundred questions. You promise to ask your uncle for a video.
The eagle on the screen reminds you of the mountains.

title: Osh and the holy mountain
text: You tell a friend about your city, Osh, one of the oldest in Central Asia, and the Sulaiman-Too mountain on a UNESCO list.

choices.t: Describe the bazaar and the mountain
choices.then: She says: "I know only Moscow. Your world is so big."
A mountain rising from the city. She looks for a long time.

title: Beshbarmak for guests
text: Your guests want to try beshbarmak, "five fingers", a dish of boiled meat and noodles that is eaten by hand.

choices.t: Cook it and teach them to eat
choices.then: There is laughter, greasy fingers and a long toast.

choices.t: Order from a Central Asian restaurant
choices.then: Quick and good.

title: Nooruz in Moscow
text: Spring arrives, and with it Nooruz. The Kyrgyz community plans a gathering with songs and a long table.

choices.then: You meet a cousin of a cousin and the evening turns into a chain of introductions.
Your family's voices warm the room.

title: Boorsok for a rainy day
text: Rain outside. You decide to fry boorsok, the golden puffs of dough you ate as a child.

choices.then: The smell travels up and down the staircase. Neighbours knock.
No regrets.

title: The EAEU advantage
text: A friend from another country asks why you do not need a patent. You explain the EAEU: citizens of member states can work without one.

choices.t: Explain the rules and offer to help him
choices.then: He is relieved to learn what is possible. You compare notes on documents.
He nods and asks someone else.

title: The jollof rice argument
text: Your classmates from Ghana say their jollof rice is better. You know that the debate is a serious cultural sport.

choices.t: Cook a pot of Nigerian jollof for the dorm
choices.then: It is smoky and spicy. Even the Ghanaians admit it is good. Almost.

choices.t: Smile and say both are good
choices.then: The debate continues, as it must.

title: Movie night: Nollywood
text: You offer to show the dorm a Nollywood film, from one of the world's largest film industries by volume.

choices.t: Organise a movie night with snacks
choices.then: There is laughter, shouting at the screen and a plot twist nobody saw coming.

choices.t: Watch it alone on a laptop
choices.then: It feels like home, in a small window.

title: Afrobeat in a Kazan club
text: A DJ plays a Fela Kuti track, the music of the pioneer of Afrobeat. You find yourself dancing before you realise it.

choices.then: Fifteen people join you. The DJ nods.
You tap your foot and smile.

title: A conversation about Soyinka
text: A literature student asks which African writers you recommend. You think of Wole Soyinka, the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986.

choices.t: Recommend a play and offer to lend it
choices.then: She returns it two weeks later with a page of notes.

choices.t: Mention Chinua Achebe's "Things Fall Apart" instead
choices.then: She writes down the title. Both are good answers.

title: Traffic jokes
text: Your classmate complains about Moscow traffic. You smile: in Lagos it is called "go-slow" and can eat half a day.

choices.t: Tell the Lagos story with gestures
choices.then: Everyone laughs. Moscow traffic seems almost polite.
Different cities, similar problems.

title: An owambe in the dorm
text: It is a friend's birthday, and you propose an owambe, a big Yoruba-style party with music, food and matching outfits.

choices.t: Organise it in the common room
choices.then: Rice, music, a speaker the size of a fridge. The dorm manager arrives, listens, and stays for an hour.
Cake, tea and a playlist.

title: Pidgin in Russia
text: On the phone with a friend you slip into Nigerian Pidgin. A Russian neighbour overhears and asks what language it is.

choices.t: Explain that it is Nigerian Pidgin, an English-based language
choices.then: She tries a phrase and giggles. "Wetin dey?" she says.
Politeness in any language.

title: Your first real winter
text: Minus twenty. You remember the Harmattan, the dry dusty wind of the Nigerian dry season, and laugh: you thought that was cold.

choices.t: Buy proper winter gear and take a photo for the family group
choices.then: The family chat explodes. "You look like a cushion!" says your cousin.

choices.t: Brave it in a thin jacket
choices.then: You learn quickly.

title: Aso ebi at a wedding
text: A Nigerian friend's wedding in Moscow asks guests to wear aso ebi, matching fabric chosen by the family.

choices.then: A sea of colours in a grey city. Strangers ask for photos.
You look smart but out of the pattern.

title: Eyo on a video call
text: Your family calls from Lagos during the Eyo festival, when masquerades in white robes walk through the streets.

choices.t: Watch the festival on your phone with your family
choices.then: You see your cousin in the crowd and wave at the screen.

choices.t: Message and promise to call tomorrow
choices.then: You miss the day, but the call is kind.

title: Suya on a Kazan roof
text: A Nigerian classmate arranges a suya night on a rooftop: grilled spiced beef, onions, pepper and a speaker.

choices.then: Smoke, stories and the first stars. Russian friends ask what the spice mix is.
A happy guest.

title: A friend asks about Lagos
text: A Russian friend asks what Lagos is really like. You think carefully about how to answer.

choices.t: Tell the full story: the noise, the food, the music, the energy
choices.then: He listens for an hour. "I want to go," he says. "I will start with a map."
He nods. "Someday you will tell me."

title: Nauryz in March
text: On the spring equinox your community celebrates Nauryz, the new year of the steppe, with a soup of seven ingredients, nauryz kozhe, shared with guests.

choices.then: They taste the soup and ask why seven. "For luck, for health, for every good thing," you say.
Your family holds up a bowl to the camera.

title: A dombra in the corner
text: A friend finds a dombra, the two-stringed lute of Kazakh music, in a music shop and asks you to show how it is played.

choices.t: Play a kui, a short piece
choices.then: The rhythm sounds like galloping horses. The shop owner stops to listen.

choices.t: Say you only know a few notes
choices.then: You laugh and promise to practise.

title: Gagarin and the steppe
text: On Cosmonautics Day a colleague mentions Gagarin. You say that he flew in 1961 from Baikonur, the spaceport on the Kazakh steppe, which is still used today.

choices.t: Tell the story of the launch pad
choices.then: She had not known that the space age began in your country. "Tell me more."
The talk moves on to the weekend.

title: Beshbarmak for the guests
text: A neighbour is moving in. You decide to welcome them with beshbarmak, boiled meat on broad noodles, the dish of Kazakh hospitality.

choices.t: Cook it and invite him over
choices.then: The whole floor smells of broth. He stays two hours.

choices.t: Buy ready noodles and keep it simple
choices.then: Not the same, but kind.

title: Who is Abai?
text: A street in Moscow carries the name of Abai, the 19th-century Kazakh poet and thinker. A friend asks who he was.

choices.then: You translate on the fly. He asks you to write the name down.

choices.t: Say it is a long story
choices.then: You promise to tell it over tea.

title: The capital on the steppe
text: A colleague asks about the capital. You explain that Astana was built on open steppe in the 1990s, and show the Baiterek tower on your phone.

choices.t: Show photos of the new skyline
choices.then: Glass towers in a flat landscape. "That is not what I imagined," he says.

choices.t: Share a picture of Almaty and the mountains
choices.then: The snow peaks above the city surprise him.

title: The mountain on the label
text: A friend holds up a bottle with Mount Ararat on the label. You say that you can see the mountain from Yerevan on a clear day.

choices.t: Tell what it means to you
choices.then: It stands across the border now, but every child in Armenia knows it. He listens quietly.
He nods and pours the tea.

title: An alphabet with a date
text: A colleague is curious about the curly Armenian letters on your keychain. You explain that Mesrop Mashtots created the alphabet around the year 405.

choices.then: She frames the note and puts it on her desk.

choices.t: Say it is a long story
choices.then: You promise to explain later.

title: Lavash from the oven
text: You find lavash, the thin flatbread baked in a clay oven. Armenian lavash is on the UNESCO list of cultural heritage.

choices.t: Buy some and share it with the office
choices.then: Wrapped around cheese and herbs, it vanishes in minutes.
Taste of your grandmother's kitchen.

title: The sound of the duduk
text: A film in the evening has music played on the duduk, the wooden double-reed pipe made of apricot wood. You recognise it from the first note.

choices.t: Tell your friends where it comes from
choices.then: The sad, warm sound fills the room. "Can you find us more of this?"

choices.t: Listen alone with the lights off
choices.then: You think of the street where you grew up.

title: A stone cross at the church
text: A friend notices a picture of a khachkar, a carved stone cross, in your room. These carved crosses are also a UNESCO heritage in Armenia.

choices.then: No two are the same, and each has its own lace of stone.

choices.t: Say it is a gift from a cousin
choices.then: He smiles and asks no more.

title: The first Christian state
text: In a talk about religion a colleague says she did not know that Armenia adopted Christianity as the state religion in 301, earlier than any other country.

choices.t: Add a few words and a story
choices.then: She asks if there are Armenian churches in Moscow. There are.
You smile and drink your tea.

title: Draniki on a cold morning
text: It is cold, and you want draniki, the potato pancakes that Belarusians eat with sour cream.

choices.t: Make a big pan for your flatmates
choices.then: They had no idea that potatoes could taste like this.

choices.t: Buy ready-made ones and eat them in silence
choices.then: It is almost the same, almost.

title: Kupalle night
text: In July friends ask about Kupalle, the midsummer night when people jump over fires and look for the fern flower in the legend.

choices.then: They are charmed by the fern flower. "Let's jump over a campfire."

choices.t: Say it is mostly songs now
choices.then: They ask you to sing, and you do.

title: The bison of Belovezhskaya Pushcha
text: A friend shows a photo of a bison. You say the Belovezhskaya Pushcha forest on the border with Poland is home to Europe's largest herd and is a UNESCO site.

choices.then: Oaks several centuries old and a quiet you cannot find in Moscow.

choices.t: Say you have been there once as a child
choices.then: The memory is warm.

title: A castle on a postcard
text: You send a postcard with the Mir castle, a UNESCO site, to a colleague who is going on holiday.

choices.then: She puts it on the fridge.
The castle stays on your wall.

title: The painter from Vitebsk
text: In a gallery a friend stops at a painting by Marc Chagall. You say that he was born near Vitebsk.

choices.then: Flying lovers and little houses suddenly look more familiar.

choices.t: Say it is true, but you know little
choices.then: You promise to read about it.

title: Two state languages
text: A colleague asks why you switch between Russian and Belarusian when you call home. Both are state languages in Belarus.

choices.then: He is surprised by how naturally you do it.

choices.t: Switch to Russian and say nothing
choices.then: He thinks you are shy.

title: Novruz at the table
text: In March you prepare for Novruz: green wheat sprouts, sweet pakhlava and shakarbura, and a table that waits for guests.

choices.then: A fire, sweets and a lot of tea. They stay late.
The phone on the table shows the whole family.

title: Mugham on an old record
