text: You find a recording of mugham, the improvised classical music of Azerbaijan that is on the UNESCO list.

choices.then: Long and slow, then suddenly intense. One of them asks for the name of the singer.

choices.t: Listen alone with the window open
choices.then: You are in your grandfather's courtyard.

title: The Old City of Baku
text: A friend sees a photo of the Maiden Tower in the Old City of Baku, a UNESCO site, and asks about it.

choices.t: Tell the legends of the tower
choices.then: Stone walls by the sea. "I want to see the city," she says.

choices.t: Share a photo of the boulevard instead
choices.then: It looks like a southern city on the sea.

title: Tea in the armudu glass
text: At the office you bring tea. In Azerbaijan it is served in an armudu, a small pear-shaped glass.

choices.then: The small glasses make the tea break feel like a ritual.
It is only tea.

title: Plov, Azerbaijani style
text: You cook plov. In Azerbaijan the rice and the meat are often served separately, with a golden crust of bread or saffron.

choices.t: Show the crust and the saffron
choices.then: The crust disappears first.

choices.t: Mix it all, like in the canteen
choices.then: Nobody complains.

title: The land of fire
text: A documentary about the Absheron peninsula shows the burning hillside Yanar Dag. A friend asks if it is real.

choices.t: Say it is real, and why
choices.then: Natural gas has been burning there for years. They are fascinated.

choices.t: Say you saw it as a child
choices.then: The memory is warm and a little scary.

title: A red and white string
text: On 1 March you tie a martisor, a red and white string, to the wrist of a friend. The custom is on the UNESCO list.

choices.t: Give one to everyone in the office
choices.then: They wear the strings for a week. Someone asks what the colours mean.

choices.t: Give one to your mother by post
choices.then: She ties it on her wrist.

title: Mamaliga with brynza
text: You make mamaliga, a thick cornmeal porridge, and serve it with cheese and sour cream, as at home.

choices.then: They had never eaten anything so simple and so warm.
It tastes better than you remembered.

title: A country of wine cellars
text: A friend asks if it is true that Moldova has cellars where the streets are underground. Milestii Mici is one of the largest wine collections in the world.

choices.then: Kilometres of tunnels and millions of bottles. "I want to go."

choices.t: Say it is true, and nothing else
choices.then: He nods and writes it down.

title: The wine festival in autumn
text: In October there is a wine festival at home. The cousins send photos of grapes, songs and a long table.

choices.t: Call and join the table by video
choices.then: A toast to the screen, and the whole kitchen laughs.
It hurts a little more than it should.

title: A hora in the park
text: At a folk festival in the park people form a ring for the hora, a circle dance. You know the steps.

choices.t: Join the circle and teach a few steps
choices.then: By the third round strangers are laughing with you.
Your feet move on their own.

title: Placinta for a rainy day
text: Rain outside. You fry placinta, the thin pies with cheese or pumpkin that you ate as a child.

choices.then: She brings jam in return.

choices.t: Eat them while you call home
choices.then: Your mother tells you what to change in the dough.

title: The horse of gold
text: A friend shows a photo of a horse with a metallic shine. You say it is an Akhal-Teke, a breed from Turkmenistan, and a national symbol.

choices.t: Tell about the horses at home
choices.then: Slim, fast and shiny in the sun. He asks if he can see one.

choices.t: Say you have only seen them from afar
choices.then: He nods and says nothing.

title: A carpet on the wall
text: Your room has a small Turkmen carpet with red patterns. A friend asks about the pattern.

choices.t: Explain the guls, the round motifs
choices.then: Each tribe has its own gul. He sees it differently now.

choices.t: Say it is a family thing
choices.then: He says he understands.

title: The door in the desert
text: A video shows the Darvaza gas crater in the Karakum desert, burning for decades. Colleagues ask if it is real.

choices.then: It was lit long ago by geologists. They watch the video three times.

choices.t: Say you have not been there
choices.then: It is far from where you grew up.

title: Melon day
text: In August Turkmenistan celebrates Melon Day. At a market you see a ripe melon that looks like the ones from home.

choices.then: Sweet and cold. "It is the best melon in Moscow," a colleague says.
It cannot be the same.

title: The white city
text: A friend finds photos of Ashgabat: white marble buildings and wide empty streets. "Is it really so white?" he asks.

choices.then: Clean, quiet and strange. He wants to see it.

choices.t: Say it is better in winter
choices.then: You smile at your own joke.

title: The sound of the dutar
text: A recording of a dutar, a two-stringed lute, plays in a Central Asian cafe. You recognise the song.

choices.t: Tell the cafe owner you know it
choices.then: He pours you tea and talks to you in Turkmen for ten minutes.
It is enough for today.

title: Which side of the escalator?
text: You step onto the metro escalator and stop in the middle. Behind you somebody sighs loudly.

choices.t: Move to the right and let people pass on the left
choices.then: Everyone flows around you. The unwritten rule is simple: stand right, walk left.
A man with a briefcase squeezes past and mutters. You learn the rule the hard way.

title: Rush-hour announcement
text: At 8:40 a voice on the loudspeaker asks everyone to stand on both sides of the escalator. People look confused.

choices.t: Stand on the left like everyone else
choices.then: The crowd moves smoothly. Safety first when it is crowded.
You are stopped by a wall of coats and a stern attendant.

title: Giving up your seat
text: The train is crowded. An older woman with two bags gets on at the next station and stands near you.

choices.then: She says thank you three times and tells you which station is best for the market.
You feel her presence all the way to the next stop.

title: A backpack in a crowded carriage
text: In the crush you realise your large backpack is hitting the people behind you.

choices.t: Take it off and hold it in front of you
choices.then: Several people nod. It is a small courtesy that makes the ride calmer.

choices.t: Leave it on, there is no room
choices.then: A few elbows remind you.

title: The wrong direction
text: You fall asleep for two stops and wake up going away from your destination.

choices.t: Get off, cross the platform and take the other train
choices.then: It costs twenty minutes. You use the time to read the station names aloud.

choices.t: Ride to the terminus and come back
choices.then: You see the end of the line, which is a very quiet place.

title: Which exit?
text: Your station has eight exits and the street signs are small. A map app says "go north".

choices.t: Look for the exit plan on the wall
choices.then: The plan shows streets, malls and bus stops. You surface at exactly the right door.

choices.t: Take the nearest exit and hope
choices.then: You come out on the wrong side of a six-lane road.

title: Mind the gap
text: The recorded voice says "Stand clear of the closing doors". A tourist holds the door with his bag.

choices.t: Gently remind him to step back
choices.then: He apologises. The train leaves on time.
The doors close on your coat for a moment. Embarrassing.

title: A station like a palace
text: You exit a station with chandeliers and mosaics and realise you have walked past them for weeks.

choices.t: Stop and look up for five minutes
choices.then: Mosaics of workers, pilots and wheat. A guard smiles: "Everybody does this once."
The ceiling will wait.

title: The Moscow Central Circle
text: A colleague tells you to use the MCC, the 54-kilometre ring railway that opened in 2016, to avoid the crowded centre.

choices.t: Try the ring for your next trip
choices.then: Overground, daylight and a map on the door. You transfer between metro lines without going downtown.

choices.t: Stay with the usual metro line
choices.then: Familiar but crowded.

title: The Central Diameters
text: You need to go to a town in the suburbs. A map app suggests the MCD (Central Diameters), launched in 2019, which run like a metro across the city and out into the region.

choices.then: Frequent trains, a clear map and a view of birch woods. You pay with your usual card.

choices.t: Take a suburban train the old way
choices.then: Slower, with a paper timetable and a dozen stops.

title: The airport train
text: You need to get to the airport. Taxis are expensive and the roads are jammed.

choices.t: Take the airport express train from a central station
choices.then: Thirty-five minutes, clean seats, no traffic. You arrive calm.
Faster in theory; in practice an hour in traffic.

title: Interchanges
text: The map shows a transfer between two stations with different names, connected by a long underground passage.

choices.then: Walk, walk, escalator: you reach the other line in six minutes.
A student walks you all the way there, talking about her thesis.

title: The marshrutka
text: A shared minibus pulls over. The driver shouts the route: "Metro, hospital, market!"

choices.t: Pay the driver and say your stop out loud
choices.then: You pass money hand to hand to the front and the change returns the same way. "Next stop, please!" and the bus stops.

choices.t: Wait for a bus with a ticket machine
choices.then: A comfortable ride, twenty minutes later.

title: A tram in the snow
text: The tram creaks slowly through the snow. Windows are frosted and the driver announces stops in a tired voice.

choices.t: Sit by the heater and count the stops
choices.then: You feel like a character in an old film.

choices.t: Get off and walk to warm up
choices.then: Five minutes in the cold feels longer than the tram.

title: The card did not read
text: You tap your travel card at the gate and the light turns red. The queue behind you grows.

choices.t: Step aside, try again, then ask the attendant
choices.then: She reloads the card in a minute and waves you through.

choices.t: Pay a single fare in cash instead
choices.then: It costs more, but the queue moves on.

title: The last bus
text: You miss the last metro. A night bus leaves in forty minutes, a taxi is three times the price.

choices.t: Wait for the night bus with a thermos of tea
choices.then: A quiet bench, a few other night-owls and a conductor who calls everyone "dear".
Home in fifteen minutes, a lighter wallet.

title: An electric scooter
text: In summer, rental scooters stand at every corner. A friend says it is the fastest way across the park.

choices.t: Rent one and keep to the bike lane
choices.then: A quick breeze and a smile. You return it on time.
You walk, you think, you arrive.

title: City bike
text: A bike-sharing station stands next to your door and the weather is mild.

choices.then: Fifteen minutes through side streets, wind in your face.
Warmer and more predictable.

title: A tram conductor
text: On an old tram a conductor walks through the carriage selling tickets and asks, "Did you pay, young person?"

choices.then: She nods and moves on.
She tears a paper ticket and says "have a good trip".

title: Surge pricing
text: A snowstorm begins and the taxi app doubles its prices. Your phone shows three minutes to wait.

choices.t: Wait ten minutes for the surge to calm
choices.then: The price falls to normal. Patience pays.
Home quickly, but your wallet complains.

title: The suburban train
text: To visit a friend outside the city you take a suburban train (elektrichka) with wooden-looking seats and vendors selling gloves and ice cream.

choices.t: Sit by the window and enjoy the ride
choices.then: Villages, birch trees, level crossings. A vendor sells you a warm pie.

choices.t: Spend the ride on your phone
choices.then: You miss the best bit of the view.

title: The timetable you cannot read
text: The paper timetable at the stop is a grid of numbers with letters and footnotes.

choices.t: Ask the driver or check a maps app
choices.then: The driver reads it for you: the bus comes every 20 minutes on weekdays, hourly on Sundays.
Forty minutes later a bus arrives. It is the wrong one.

title: Lunch in the canteen
text: The canteen offers soup, a cutlet with buckwheat and compote for ₽250. Colleagues wave you over to their table.

choices.then: You hear who is getting married and whose boss is leaving. Information is the real dessert.
A quiet half hour.

title: A birthday cake
text: A colleague brings a cake for her birthday and a card goes around for signatures.

choices.t: Sign the card and add ₽300 to the gift
choices.then: You are thanked by name. Cake tastes better with a good conscience.

choices.t: Take a slice and say congratulations
choices.then: She smiles. It is enough.

title: Payday
text: The accountant puts the envelope (or the transfer) through. The mood in the workshop improves by about forty percent.

choices.t: Treat the team to tea and sweets
choices.then: A tradition: the first to say "payday" buys the cookies.
You count it twice and relax.

title: Safety briefing
text: Every quarter the supervisor reads the safety rules aloud for twenty minutes. Half of the room is asleep.

choices.t: Listen and ask one real question
choices.then: The supervisor brightens: "At last, a question." The answer might save you one day.
Twenty minutes, one signature.

title: A training afternoon
text: Management organises a half-day course on customer service and teamwork, with a slide show and free tea.

choices.then: You pick up two useful ideas and one terrible joke.
You absorb about ten percent.

title: Shift swap
text: A colleague asks you to swap shifts so he can attend his daughter's concert on Saturday.

choices.then: He owes you one, and says so three times.
He finds someone else. You feel a little small.

title: Late because of the snow
text: Buses are delayed by snow and you arrive twenty minutes after your shift starts.

choices.t: Apologise and make up the time
choices.then: Your supervisor nods; you stay late and nobody mentions it again.
It is true, and the supervisor sighs: "Everybody is late today."

title: A very hot day at work
text: It is thirty-four degrees and the ventilation is broken. Water bottles disappear by 11 a.m.

choices.t: Bring ice and water for the team
choices.then: Cold bottles are passed around. You are the hero of the afternoon.
You survive.

title: Praise from the manager
text: At the morning meeting the manager says, unexpectedly, that your work has been "reliable and neat".

choices.t: Thank him and credit the team
choices.then: Colleagues smile. Credit shared is credit doubled.
You feel warm all day.

title: Layoff rumours
text: Whispers say the company will cut staff after New Year. Everyone looks at the management corridor.

choices.then: He says: "Nothing is decided. Do good work." It is more honest than reassuring.
Just in case. You feel better having a plan.

title: A missing tool
text: The tool (or the key, or the scanner) you need has disappeared from its place.

choices.t: Search methodically and ask who used it last
choices.then: It is found in a jacket pocket. Fifteen minutes lost, a lesson gained.

choices.t: Borrow from the next team and say nothing
choices.then: Quick, but they notice.

title: Tea on the night shift
text: At 3 a.m. the building is quiet. Someone boils a kettle and a half-circle of tired faces gathers.

choices.t: Join them and listen to the stories
choices.then: Two hours of dry jokes and good advice. You learn more than in the day.
You finish on time and are the first to leave.

title: A new uniform
text: Management hands out new uniforms and hats with the company logo. Nobody asked for the hat.

choices.then: The hat is surprisingly warm. Customers are impressed by the logo.

choices.t: Wear your old clothes under it
choices.then: You are the only one.

title: A medical book check
text: The employer asks every employee to renew their medical book (sanitary book), which takes a day and some money.

choices.then: Queues and stamps, but you have the paper before the inspection.
The inspector arrives sooner than expected.

title: A customer says thank you
text: A customer returns just to say that your help yesterday made her day.

choices.t: Smile and say it was nothing
choices.then: She leaves a small chocolate. You carry the smile for hours.
He writes it on the notice board with a star.

title: Two words that mean the same
text: Your colleagues argue over whether the word you used is "correct" Russian or only used in some regions.

choices.t: Join the debate with a local example
choices.then: Half the room learns a new word and half teaches you one back.
Wisdom of the quiet colleague.

title: The radio in the workshop
text: The radio plays the same eight songs, and you now know all the words.

choices.then: By lunch the whole room is humming. Productivity goes up or down, depending on who you ask.
Your own playlist for your own thoughts.

title: The corner by the door
text: Colleagues gather in the cold corner behind the building for a break, whether they smoke or not.

choices.t: Join them with a cup of tea
choices.then: It is where the real decisions are made.
You miss one rumour.

title: The staff photograph
text: The company is making a poster with employee portraits and asks for volunteers.

choices.then: You look like a stranger in a tie. Your mother will love it.
Others take the slot.

title: The form for the form
text: HR asks you to fill in a form about the form you filled in last month. Rewrite, sign and return.

choices.then: It takes twenty minutes and saves you a longer conversation later.
HR sends a polite reminder every day.

title: The boss's boss arrives
text: A director from head office tours the site. Everything is suddenly very clean.

choices.t: Stay calm and do your usual work
choices.then: He nods at your corner and moves on. No drama.
It looks good, until you find the broom behind the door.

title: The nurse visits
text: Within three days of leaving the maternity hospital, a nurse from the children's clinic rings your bell with a bag, a scale and a long list of questions. Later a paediatrician comes too.

choices.then: She weighs the baby, shows you how to bathe and swaddle, and leaves her phone number. You feel less alone.

choices.t: Let her do her check and listen
choices.then: She is quick and kind. You will remember half of what she said.

title: Vaccination day
text: The national calendar gives vaccines at birth, in the first week, and again at 3, 4.5 and 6 months. Today it is the three-month check at the polyclinic.

choices.t: Go on time with the card and wait in the queue
choices.then: The nurse is quick, the baby cries for a minute and then falls asleep on your shoulder.

choices.t: Ask the paediatrician to explain every shot first
choices.then: Twenty minutes of calm explanations. You leave sure of your decision.

title: Sleepless nights
text: Three nights in a row the baby wakes every ninety minutes. The kettle is your best friend.

choices.then: You sleep four hours in a block. It feels like a holiday.

choices.t: Do it alone and push through
choices.then: You are a zombie at work and the world looks slightly underwater.

title: The childcare allowance
text: A colleague says that the working parent of a child under one and a half years can receive a monthly allowance of 40% of average earnings, paid to one parent only.

choices.t: Apply through your employer and the portal
choices.then: Forms, certificates, a birth certificate copy and a bank account. A month later the first payment arrives (simplified in the game: a fixed weekly amount).
You tell yourself it is not worth the queue. Your partner shakes their head.

title: The first real smile
text: At six in the morning the baby looks at you and smiles for the first time. It is not gas. You are almost sure.

choices.t: Wake your partner to see it
choices.then: The smile has gone, but the moment stays with both of you.
You hold your breath until the baby falls asleep.

title: First solid foods
text: At six months the paediatrician suggests starting solids: a teaspoon of puree, a lot of mess and a bib.

choices.then: Steamed pumpkin and a blender. Half ends up on the wall.
Easy and clean, and the baby makes a face of deep suspicion.

title: A stroller in the snow
text: Pavements are covered in snow and the stroller has the wrong wheels. The entrance has five steps.

choices.t: Ask a neighbour to help carry it
choices.then: Two minutes later a stranger lifts it and says "of course". Neighbours are useful.
Your back complains, the baby sleeps against your chest, and you cross the courtyard like an expert.

title: The first winter
text: The baby needs an overall, a hat, mittens and a blanket, and a surprising number of layers.

choices.then: Warm, soft, slightly too large. The baby will grow into it by February.

choices.t: Borrow from a friend with a bigger baby
choices.then: A bag of second-hand clothes arrives with a note: "pass it on afterwards".

title: Nursery, nanny or grandparents?
text: You are going back to work soon. Someone has to look after the baby for eight hours a day.

choices.then: A kind woman in her fifties who sings old lullabies. The baby adores her.
They arrive with six bags of food and firm views on feeding. It works, mostly.

title: The first tooth
text: The baby chews everything, drools constantly and cries at night. A tooth is on its way.

choices.then: Two days later: a tiny white edge and a proud, toothless grin.
She says it is normal and shows you how to massage the gums.

title: Grandmother visits
text: Your mother (or your partner's) arrives with a huge bag, a cooked chicken and a lot of advice.

choices.t: Listen politely and accept the help
choices.then: The flat is cleaner than it has been for weeks. You sleep three hours straight.

choices.t: Politely explain that things have changed
choices.then: A short silence and then a nod. She still cooks the chicken.

title: First steps
text: The baby lets go of the sofa, takes three wobbly steps and falls into your arms.

choices.t: Cheer as if it were a national holiday
choices.then: The neighbours hear the shouting and wonder what happened. Nothing matters but this.

choices.t: Film it for the family chat
choices.then: Thirty-eight hearts and a message from Grandpa: "Genius, like his father".

title: The parents' chat
text: A messenger group of local parents buzzes with advice on colic, cough syrup and the best playground.

choices.then: Fourteen answers in ten minutes, three of them contradictory, one very good.
Silence. You miss the useful tip about the free clinic day.

title: The playground
text: A small playground in the courtyard, with swings, a sandbox and mothers, fathers and grandmothers on benches comparing notes.

choices.then: Within an hour you know three secrets about the neighbourhood and the best baby sleep trick.

choices.t: Push the swing and keep to yourself
choices.then: A quiet hour in the fresh air.

title: The gradebook (zachetka)
text: The dean's office hands you a small booklet, your zachetka. Every credit and every exam grade goes into it, signed by the teacher.

choices.t: Keep it carefully and bring it to every exam
choices.then: A tidy booklet means no panic at the dean's office. You are a person of order.
A week before the session you find it under a pile of notes, a bit crumpled.

title: A pass without an exam: the "avtomat"
text: The professor announces: "Those who attended every lecture and handed in all assignments get the grade automatically."

choices.then: You get the grade at once. A whole week free of cramming.

choices.t: Say you would rather sit the exam to improve the grade
choices.then: The professor is surprised, then pleased. You do the exam and score higher.

title: A week of deadlines (zapara)
text: Three assignments, a presentation and a laboratory report are due in the same week. The corridor smells of instant noodles and panic.

choices.t: Plan every day by the hour and sleep in shifts
choices.then: It hurts, but everything is handed in. You discover the power of a to-do list.

choices.t: Ask for an extension on one of them
choices.then: The teacher grants two days. One less knot in your stomach.

title: The pass at the dormitory door
text: The dormitory guard asks for your pass at the entrance every evening. "No pass, no entry," she says, not unkindly.

choices.t: Show it with a smile and say good evening
choices.then: She nods. Within a month she lets you in even when you forget it, and asks how the exam went.
She looks over her glasses. It takes ten minutes and a phone call to the warden.

title: The shared kitchen
text: One kitchen per floor, one rota, one fridge with names written on tape. Someone has been eating other people's dumplings.

choices.t: Propose a cleaning rota and name labels
choices.then: The floor meeting is stormy, then peaceful. The rota survives for three weeks, a record.

choices.t: Cook late at night when nobody is there
choices.then: Quiet and efficient, if a little lonely.

title: Quiet hours
text: It is midnight and somebody is playing the guitar loudly in the next room before an exam.

choices.t: Knock politely and ask them to stop
choices.then: The guitar falls silent. The next day a note appears: "Sorry. Good luck on the exam!"
You study to a distant chorus of "Kino". You learn a new song.

title: Coursework
text: Your coursework (kursovaya) is due: twenty pages, a bibliography and a supervisor who answers messages only on Tuesdays.

choices.t: Start early and book supervision slots
choices.then: You hand in on time and the supervisor writes "good work" in the margin.

choices.t: Write it all in the last two nights
choices.then: A grey dawn, strong tea and a text that you hope nobody reads too closely.

title: A "tail" (khvost)
text: You failed one exam in the session. In student speech this is a khvost, a tail: a debt that follows you until you retake it.

choices.t: Prepare properly and retake it this week
choices.then: You pass at the second attempt and feel the tail drop off.

choices.t: Put it off until next term
choices.then: The tail grows heavier. The dean's office sends a polite warning.

title: The group leader (starosta)
text: The group elects a starosta, a student who passes messages between the group and the dean's office. Nobody wants the job, and everyone looks at you.

choices.then: You get the schedule first, the blame second and a small respect from the dean's office.

choices.t: Propose a colleague who is good with messages
choices.then: A relieved classmate says yes. You owe each other a coffee.

title: The student council
text: The student council organises a trip, a concert and a clean-up day. They need volunteers with a free weekend.

choices.then: Gloves, bags and tea at noon. A dozen new friends.

choices.t: Buy a ticket for the concert instead
choices.then: Loud, crowded, lovely. Your voice is gone by Monday.

title: Work placement (praktika)
text: The programme requires a two-week placement at a company. A list of partner firms is on the notice board.

choices.t: Choose a firm in your field and apply
choices.then: You learn more in two weeks than in two terms. The supervisor writes you a kind reference.

choices.t: Pick the nearest one, whatever it does
choices.then: You file papers and learn how an office coffee machine works.

title: Scholarship day
text: On the 25th the scholarship arrives: a modest sum, welcome as rain after a drought. Students joke that it is enough for tea.

choices.t: Budget it for the month in an app
choices.then: You track every rouble. You are surprised how far it goes.

choices.t: Spend half of it on a pizza evening
choices.then: Twelve people, three pizzas and a rule: nobody mentions the exam.

title: Choosing a thesis topic
text: The department publishes a list of topics for final theses and supervisors. Some of them are famous and strict.

choices.t: Pick a topic that excites you, even if it is hard
choices.then: The supervisor smiles: "At last, somebody who wants to work."
You will finish early and be a little bored.

title: Dorm registration check
text: The university's international office checks that every foreign student's migration registration is valid before the term continues.

choices.t: Bring your passport, card and registration copies
choices.then: The officer stamps a list and smiles. Everything is in order.

choices.t: Realise your registration is about to expire
choices.then: She walks you to the right window and helps you start the renewal at once.

title: A leaflet about your rights
text: In the international office a leaflet from the university legal clinic lies on the table: "What to do if the police ask for your documents". It has a checklist and the phone numbers of your embassy and a volunteer lawyer.

choices.t: Read it carefully and keep it in your bag
choices.then: You learn what to carry (original passport, migration card, registration), that you may ask the grounds for a check, ask for an interpreter, and refuse to sign what you do not understand. You photograph the phone numbers.

choices.t: Take it and read it later
choices.then: It stays in the bag until it is too crumpled to read.

title: Only a photo of the passport
text: At a metro entrance an officer asks for documents. You have a photo of your passport on your phone but the original is at home.

choices.t: Show the photo and explain politely
choices.then: The officer says that foreigners must carry the original, migration card and registration. He lets you off with a warning, this time.

choices.t: Call a flatmate to bring the original to the station
choices.then: It takes forty minutes and a lot of explaining, but nothing is written down.

title: Why are you asking?
text: An officer stops you in the street and asks for documents. You are not sure that he has any reason.

choices.t: Show the documents and politely ask the grounds for the check
choices.then: He says there was a complaint about a person who looks similar. He thanks you, checks the documents and lets you go.
This turns a two-minute check into an hour at the station.

title: The protocol in fast Russian
text: An officer starts writing a protocol and reads it out very fast. You understand about a third.

choices.t: Say clearly that you need an interpreter
choices.then: They call one. It takes an hour, but you understand everything you are asked to sign.
You sign something you did not understand. Your stomach sinks as you leave.

title: A paper to sign
text: You are asked to sign a statement. It says you agree with the violation, which you do not.

choices.t: Refuse to sign what you disagree with and write down your objection
choices.then: The officer sighs, adds your comment to the record and lets you go. You also ask for a copy.
You are home in ten minutes with a fine you could have contested.

title: Detained for a few hours
text: After a check you are taken to the station. Nobody tells you how long it will last, and your phone is switched off. (A university guide for international students says you may ask to tell a family member or a friend about your detention within three hours.)

choices.t: Ask politely to tell a friend or family member where you are, and to contact your consulate
choices.then: Within three hours a friend knows where you are and a volunteer lawyer calls the station. They let you go in the evening.
Five hours of silence on a plastic chair. You are released at midnight with a pale face.

title: A search of your bag
text: An officer opens your bag and starts to take things out in the street, with nobody else around.

choices.t: Calmly ask for two witnesses and for it to be written down
choices.then: The officer pauses. Two bystanders are called, a short record is made and nothing is found.
He finds your lunch, your charger and a lot of embarrassment.

title: Opening the dacha season
text: A colleague invites you to help open her dacha for the summer: unlock the shed, uncover the beds, find out what the winter did to the roof.

choices.t: Go on Saturday with a spade
choices.then: Dust, spiders and a cup of tea from a thermos on the porch. A good first day of summer.
She sighs and asks again in June.

title: Planting potatoes
text: The traditional early-May task: potatoes go into the ground, and a whole family tries to explain what the right depth is.

choices.then: Rows, laughter and blisters. In autumn you will eat what you planted.

choices.t: Make the tea for the diggers
choices.then: Respectable, light work. Nobody says anything.

title: The Friday elektrichka
text: On Friday evening the suburban train is full of people with spades, seedlings, cool-boxes and cats in carriers.

choices.t: Squeeze in and enjoy the show
choices.then: Standing for an hour, you meet a man who knows everything about tomatoes.
It is just as crowded, but you get a seat by the window.

title: Six sotok
text: A friend proudly shows you around his 600 square metres: "Six sotok! A real farm!" There are two tomato beds, an apple tree and a hammock.

choices.then: He talks about each tomato variety for twenty minutes. You leave with seedlings.
The best idea anyone has had all week.

title: The greenhouse
text: The greenhouse is an oven in July. Tomatoes redden, cucumbers hang down like green fingers.

choices.t: Water, pick and tie up the plants
choices.then: You return with a bucket of vegetables and a farmer's tan.
You eat his tomatoes later anyway.

title: Mosquitoes at dusk
text: At eight o'clock the sun sinks and the mosquitoes rise in clouds. Everyone on the porch swats and complains.

choices.t: Light a smoky fire and sit by it
choices.then: Smoke in your eyes, but nobody gets bitten. Stories begin.
The mosquitoes tap on the window like critics.

title: The dacha banya
text: There is a small wooden banya at the end of the garden. The host stokes the stove and hands out birch twigs.

choices.t: Steam properly and then jump in the cold water
choices.then: Pink, giddy and perfectly calm.

choices.t: Sit on the lower bench and chat
choices.then: Heat is optional, conversation is not.

title: A dispute over the fence
text: Two neighbours argue about whose apple tree hangs over whose fence. Both look at you for a verdict.

choices.t: Suggest sharing the apples and finishing the tea
choices.then: The apples are divided, the fence stays, and they shake hands.
Wise, if cowardly.

title: Berries and jam
text: Raspberries, currants and strawberries are ripe, and a huge pot of jam stands on the stove with its sticky aroma.

choices.t: Pick, stir and fill the jars
choices.then: Twenty jars with handwritten labels. You are given three.

choices.t: Eat berries straight from the bush
choices.then: Perfectly legitimate behaviour.

title: Shashlik by the fence
text: The host marinates meat since the morning. Everyone gives advice on the grill, the charcoal and how long to wait.

choices.then: Smoke, sparks and perfect skewers. You are given applause and a plate.
The most important job: you chop onions until your eyes weep.

title: Harvest and pickling
text: In late August cucumbers, dill and garlic fill the kitchen. Jars, brine and old recipes are everywhere.

choices.t: Pickle cucumbers with the family recipe
choices.then: The kitchen smells of dill and garlic. In January you will thank yourself.

choices.t: Take a bag of fresh vegetables home
choices.then: Generosity is its own reward.

title: Closing the dacha for winter
text: In October the water is shut off, the pipes drained, the plants covered and the shed locked until spring.

choices.t: Do it carefully with the owner
choices.then: You sip tea on a bare porch, as leaves fall. The garden sleeps.

choices.t: Send your regards from the city
choices.then: The garden sleeps without you.

title: A leaking roof
text: After a storm the ceiling of your village house drips. A bucket sings in the corner.

choices.t: Fix it yourself with tar paper
choices.then: Three hours on a ladder. It holds for a while, and you feel capable.
He arrives with a thermos and a grin. The roof is dry by evening.

title: Firewood for winter
text: The first frost reminds you that the stove in your village house needs wood. A neighbour sells a cartload.

choices.t: Buy a load and stack it yourself
choices.then: A tidy woodpile, an aching back and a cosy evening by the stove.

choices.t: Buy less and plan to top up
choices.then: A small pile and an optimistic mind.

title: The intercom code
text: A courier stands at the door of your block and cannot get in. The entrance code on the paper note is rubbed off.

choices.t: Come down and let him in
choices.then: He thanks you three times. Your dinner arrives hot.

choices.t: Tell him the code over the phone
choices.then: He is in within a minute. Neighbours would call this "trust".

title: The lift is out of order
text: A handwritten sign on the lift: "Not working. Repair soon." Your flat is on the ninth floor and you are carrying shopping.

choices.then: Nine floors later you know exactly how fit you are.

choices.t: Leave half downstairs with a neighbour
choices.then: A neighbour watches the bags and you chat on the stairs. Both of you complain about the management company.

title: The residents' group chat
text: There are 214 unread messages in the building chat. The topic: who parked across the entrance, again.

choices.then: Peace. You will find out about everything a week later.
You get a lot of opinions and one friendly neighbour who agrees with you.

title: The house meeting
text: A notice on the door invites owners and residents to a meeting about the courtyard fence. Chairs in the courtyard, a man with a folder, a lot of shouting.

choices.then: Three hours later the fence is neither approved nor rejected. You know everyone's name.
The result is decided without you.

title: The management company
text: A receipt arrives with a new line on it: "adjustment". You are not sure what is being adjusted.

choices.t: Go to the office and ask
choices.then: A tired clerk explains the line and corrects one number. You leave with a stamped copy.
Peaceful and slightly more expensive.

title: Drilling next door
text: It is Saturday morning and a drill is working through the wall. You know the neighbours are renovating for the third year in a row.

choices.then: The neighbour apologises and promises to stop by lunchtime. He does, mostly.
Not elegant, but quiet enough.

title: The bench by the entrance
text: The older women on the bench at the entrance have noticed you. "New? Which flat? Are you married?"

choices.then: You leave knowing the history of every flat in the block and with a jar of pickled cucumbers.
Polite. They will still discuss you for a week.

title: Water through the ceiling
text: A brown stain spreads across your ceiling. The flat above has a burst pipe and nobody answers the door.

choices.t: Call the emergency service of the UK
choices.then: A plumber arrives in an hour and shuts the riser. You photograph everything for the insurance talk later.

choices.t: Run upstairs and bang on every door
choices.then: You find the right neighbour on the third try; he is on holiday and his son comes in pyjamas.

title: The autumn clean-up day
text: A flyer in the lift invites everyone to a clean-up day: rakes, bags, and a free tea afterwards.

choices.then: You rake leaves beside people who have lived here for decades. Afterwards, tea in plastic cups.
Nobody asks you to come again, nor to stay away.

title: The neighbour's parcel
text: The courier left a neighbour's parcel with you. The neighbour is nowhere to be found.

choices.t: Leave a note on their door
choices.then: They collect it in the evening with a bar of chocolate.
It sits by your door and looks at you.

title: A call from "bank security"
text: A calm voice says your account is under attack and asks for the code from the SMS "to cancel the transfer".

choices.then: The code was the one that confirms a transfer. The money is gone before you finish the call.

choices.t: Hang up and call the number on the back of your card
choices.then: The real bank says there is no problem. Banks never ask for codes.

title: A parcel you did not order
text: An SMS says a courier cannot deliver and asks you to follow a link and enter your card number "to confirm the address".

choices.then: You type the card details. A few minutes later the card is emptied.
You check the real tracking in the shop's app: nothing is on its way.

title: A code from Gosuslugi
text: Someone calls from the "post office" and asks you to read out the code from an SMS to "extend your parcel storage".

choices.then: Hours later the account sends a loan application you never made. You spend a week undoing it.

choices.t: Say you will go to the post office in person
choices.then: The caller hangs up. Nobody ever asked for that code again.

title: The "safe account"
text: A man introduces himself as an investigator and says your money must be moved to a "safe account" right now, and that you must not tell anyone.

choices.then: You move the money. There is no investigator and no safe account.

choices.t: Say you will talk to the bank in person
choices.then: The line goes quiet and then dead. Real officials do not rush people.

title: A very keen buyer
text: You have posted something for sale online. A buyer wants to pay at once and sends a link "to receive the money safely".

choices.t: Open the buyer's link and enter your card
choices.then: There is nothing to receive. The card is charged instead.

choices.t: Meet in person or use the platform's own payment
choices.then: Slower, but the buyer vanishes and your money stays where it was.

title: A message from "the director"
text: A new contact with your director's photo writes in a messenger: urgent task, transfer a payment now, no questions.

choices.then: The payment goes to a stranger. The real director is not pleased.

choices.t: Call the director on the number you already have
choices.then: It was fake. The director thanks you for checking.

title: Your phone number "expires"
text: A voice says your SIM card contract ends today and you must confirm a code or you will lose your number.

choices.then: You hesitate: nobody loses a number like this. You hang up.
Everything is fine. You block the number.

title: The investment chat
text: You are added to a chat where members post screenshots of huge profits from an "expert" trading signals.

choices.t: Send a small deposit to try
choices.then: The "expert" asks for more; you stop and realise everyone in the chat is the same account.
Easy money did not exist yesterday and does not today.

title: The GTO badge
text: A colleague shows you a badge on his lapel: GTO, "Ready for Labour and Defence". The complex was revived in 2014, with bronze, silver and gold badges and tests for every age from six years up.

choices.then: Pull-ups, a run and a swim later, you are tired, sore and strangely proud. The paperwork says "silver".

choices.t: Say you will think about it
choices.then: He smiles. Everyone says that.

title: Football in the yard
text: On a summer evening the lads in the yard are one player short. "You! Come on!"

choices.then: Two goals, one scraped knee and a lot of new friends.
You shout advice and are mostly ignored. It is still fun.

title: Hockey on the rink
text: A friend invites you to a pick-up game at an outdoor rink: borrowed skates, borrowed stick, a lot of steam.

choices.then: You fall eleven times and score once by accident. The team applauds.
A calmer evening, a few laps, a hot tea from a thermos.

title: Cross-country skiing
text: There is a trail in the nearby park. Skis can be rented by the hour; the forest under snow is quiet and white.

choices.then: An hour in, you stop noticing the cold. You come back red-faced and happy.
The pace is slower but the air is just as good.

title: A gym membership
text: A gym near the metro offers a first month at a discount. The trainer smiles. The treadmill looks unfriendly.

choices.then: You go four times, then life interferes. You feel better anyway.
Cheap, honest and windier than you expected.

title: Chess in the courtyard
text: Two men play chess at a table in the courtyard, a small crowd watching. One of them looks up: "Play?"

choices.then: You lose in eleven moves and win a lesson on the Sicilian. You are asked to come again.
You learn more from the crowd's whispered advice than from the game.

title: Volleyball by the river
text: A group of students has put up a net on the sand by the river. A ball lands at your feet.

choices.t: Throw it back and join in
choices.then: You learn the rules from shouting. The evening ends with a shared watermelon.

choices.t: Return the ball and keep walking
choices.then: A polite wave. A normal evening.

title: Morning exercises
text: A neighbour does her morning exercises on the balcony in all weather and invites you to try "just ten minutes".

choices.then: The first days hurt, then you feel lighter. She nods: "Of course."
The most comfortable decision of the day.

title: The match on TV
text: Everyone at work is talking about last night's match. The office is split into two camps and a friendly bet is going.

choices.t: Join the debate and bet a small amount
choices.then: Whichever side wins, the coffee machine becomes a place of shared opinion.
You nod at the right moments and keep the peace.

title: The public pool
text: A public pool offers a lane for beginners. You need a cap, a medical certificate and slippers; the staff are strict about all three.

choices.then: Visits to the clinic, a stamp, then forty slow lengths. A good habit starts.
The cap stays unbought.

title: The name and the middle name
text: A clerk calls you in. She addresses the man before you as "Ivan Petrovich" and looks at you expectantly: how should she address you?

choices.t: Say your first name and your father's name
choices.then: She writes it down with a nod. Politeness in Russia is built from these three names.

choices.t: Say "just call me by my name"
choices.then: She does, with a slightly puzzled smile.

title: "Ty" or "vy"?
text: You say "ty" to a senior colleague and the room goes quiet for a second. Russian has an informal "ty" and a formal "vy", and the border is not always obvious.

choices.then: He smiles: "Nothing, I understand." Next time it will be easier.
He lets it go, but you feel that you have been placed in a category.

title: Reading the signs
text: A street sign, a menu and a pharmacy box are all in Cyrillic. You can sound out half the letters, and some of the words turn out to be English in disguise: "МЕТРО", "КАФЕ", "ТАКСИ".

choices.then: You feel like a child and then like a detective. Signs start to make sense.
Faster, but you remember nothing.

title: "Bring a certificate"
text: In an office you are told: "A certificate and a certified copy, then come back." You do not know exactly what the words mean, only that the clerk is already looking at the next person.

choices.t: Ask her to write the two words down
choices.then: She sighs and writes them. You look them up outside; the second day at the office is quick.
You spend a day guessing and a week wondering.

title: How are you?
text: A neighbour asks "Kak dela?" and you answer "fine". She tells you, kindly, that in Russia the question is sometimes meant seriously.

choices.then: Twenty minutes later she knows about your week and you know about her knees. You feel closer.
Polite and quick, though somehow lonelier.

title: Your accent
text: A shop assistant smiles when you speak and asks where you are from. It is friendly curiosity, but you sometimes wonder what comes next.

choices.t: Tell her about your home town
choices.then: She tells you where to buy the best spices in the city. A small local alliance.
She laughs: "Then you are one of us."

title: A word you do not know
text: A colleague from another region uses a local word and everyone nods. You were sure you knew Russian.

choices.then: It turns out nobody outside his region knows it either. Everyone laughs.
You nod and lose the thread of the conversation.

title: Filling in a form by hand
text: The form must be filled in capitals, in Cyrillic, with no corrections. You have one copy.

choices.t: Fill it in slowly with a ruler
choices.then: Perfect. The clerk is almost disappointed to find nothing wrong.

choices.t: Rush it and cross something out
choices.then: You start again with a new form and a new queue ticket.

title: A free language club
text: A library advertises a free Russian conversation club on Thursdays: tea, simple texts and volunteers who are patient.

choices.then: Slowly the sentences grow. You also make two friends and a homework habit.

choices.t: Study with an app at home
choices.then: Efficient and solitary.

title: A line of poetry
text: A taxi driver recites a line of Pushkin about the road and asks if you know it. In Russia, a stranger quoting a poet is not unusual.

choices.t: Admit that you do not, and ask for more
choices.then: He recites for ten minutes and recommends a book. You get out with a new reading list.
He quotes another line to the road itself.

title: The radiators are still cold
text: It is October and the mornings are frosty. Under the rules in force when the game was written, heating must start after five days in a row when the average daily temperature is below +8 °C; the neighbours are already asking when it will come.

choices.t: Wait a few days and use a heater
choices.then: On the sixth cold day the radiators begin to creak and warm up. The heater goes back into the cupboard.
You get a recorded message and then a real person: "The temperature has not yet been long enough. Soon."

title: The heating ends
text: In April the radiators go cold overnight. The rules allow switching them off after five days in a row above +8 °C, and the evening air is still sharp.

choices.t: Wear a sweater and wait for spring
choices.then: A week later the sun does the job. You no longer notice.

choices.t: Buy an electric heater for the cold evenings
choices.then: Warm, cosy and the electricity bill rises a little.

title: No hot water this summer
text: A notice in the lift: hot water will be off for planned maintenance, two weeks in summer. Many people in Russian cities know this ritual.

choices.t: Boil water in a saucepan like everyone else
choices.then: You wash in a basin and learn the exact time it takes to heat a pan.

choices.t: Stay with a friend for the two weeks
choices.then: You are hosted with tea and mild teasing. The shower is hot.

title: The meter readings
text: A reminder app says that the water meter readings must be sent this week. The meter hides behind a pipe under the sink.

choices.then: Done in ten minutes; the receipt next month is a little smaller.
The management company calculates by the average instead, and it is not in your favour.

title: The single payment receipt
text: A single payment document arrives for the flat: heating, water, electricity, the lift, the "major repairs fund". One line is higher than last month.

choices.then: It was a mistake, corrected after a polite email. You feel quietly victorious.
It is paid and the world is calm, but you wonder about that line.

title: Viewing a flat
text: An advert says "no agents, near the metro". At the viewing the owner explains all the rules of the flat in the first ten minutes: no parties, no pets, shoes off.

choices.then: The rules are strict and the neighbours are kind. A fair deal.
You see three more flats; one has a wallpaper that has seen a lot.

title: The deposit
text: The owner asks for a deposit equal to one month's rent and promises to return it at the end. You ask for a written agreement; he looks mildly offended.

choices.then: He signs after a pause. In a year you are glad.
It works out this time. The lesson is learnt by someone else.

title: The owner drops by
text: The landlord rings: "I will pop in tomorrow to check the pipes." He arrives with a bag of apples and checks everything, including the cupboards.

choices.t: Show him round and offer tea
choices.then: He leaves in good mood and the rent stays the same for another year.

choices.t: Say you are not at home
choices.then: He sighs and comes back at the weekend.

title: A cold flat in winter
text: In January the radiators are lukewarm and the room is 16 degrees. You feel your breath near the window.

choices.t: Write a complaint to the management company
choices.then: Within days a plumber bleeds the air from the radiators. Real warmth.

choices.t: Seal the window with tape and a blanket
choices.then: Not elegant but a warm night.

title: The neighbour above has a sink problem
text: Brown water drips from the light fitting in the corridor. The neighbour above says "Oh, thank you for telling me" and goes to find the plumber.

choices.t: Photograph the damage and write a note for the record
choices.then: The neighbour pays for the repair without drama; the note was enough.
A peaceful evening. The ceiling will tell its story later.

title: The advance and the salary
text: Your company pays twice a month: the "advance" in the second half of the month and the "salary" at the start of the next. The advance is smaller and arrives first.

choices.t: Plan the month around both payments
choices.then: Rent from the salary, food from the advance. It works, and for once you know where the money is.
A good dinner, a bad week.

title: Payday on a Sunday
text: Payday falls on a Sunday. A colleague says the company must pay it on the day before, and the accountant, to your surprise, agrees.

choices.t: Wait for Friday and keep your plans
choices.then: On Friday evening the notification arrives. The rule works.
The accountant says no gently; you come back on Friday.

title: The pay slip
text: You receive a pay slip with eleven lines and several abbreviations. The sum is not what you thought.

choices.then: She goes through every line. You leave knowing what a deduction is.

choices.t: Look only at the bottom line
choices.then: It matches the card balance. That will do for now.

title: An offer "in an envelope"
text: A small employer offers more than the market, "but part of it in an envelope, unofficial". No pension, no sick pay and no proof of income.

choices.then: The offer falls through. The next one is honest and slightly lower.
Good money until the first illness. You have no receipts for anything.

title: The salary is late again
text: Payday passes. The manager says "next week" for the second time. Colleagues whisper about complaining.

choices.t: Write a formal request to the employer
choices.then: It arrives in a document, so it cannot be forgotten. The money comes within days.
It arrives, a week late, and nobody says sorry.

title: The labour inspection
text: A colleague says you can complain online to the labour inspectorate if the employer ignores your rights. Nobody has done it yet.

choices.then: You read the instructions and keep them for later. You feel less alone.
Safe for now, and a bit uneasy.

title: Holiday pay
text: Your holiday starts next week. The accountant says holiday pay is paid before it begins, and that it is calculated from your average earnings.

choices.t: Take the holiday and plan a trip
choices.then: The pay arrives in time. A few days by water; the world feels slow.
The boss is pleased, your body is not.

title: A sick note
text: You have a high temperature. The doctor opens an electronic sick note and tells you to stay home.

choices.then: A few days under blankets. The payment for sick days comes later and is less than your pay.
You infect half the office. The boss says nothing and everyone knows.

title: Asking for a raise
text: You have worked well for a year. The boss is a person who says "we will think about it".

choices.t: Ask politely with a list of what you did
choices.then: He is surprised by the list. A raise comes in the next pay.
He notices, in a year or two.

title: Platzkart or kupe?
text: You are planning a long trip by train. A friend swears by the open-plan carriage, "platzkart": cheap, noisy and full of stories. The four-berth compartment, "kupe", has a door.

choices.then: Forty people, a baby, a guitar and a man who shares his chicken. You arrive with three new contacts.
A closed door and three quiet strangers. You sleep well.

title: The carriage attendant
text: The attendant, the "provodnitsa", stands at the door of the carriage and checks every ticket and passport as if each were a rare document.

choices.t: Greet her politely and ask about the boiler
choices.then: She shows you where the hot water is and where the bedding is kept. You are now a regular.
You find the water yourself in the end. She watches without comment.

title: Tea in a glass holder
text: On the table of the carriage the tea comes in a glass in a metal holder, and the train swings gently as it moves through the evening.

choices.t: Ask for tea and watch the fields
choices.then: Birches, villages, a dog on a station platform. Time stops being measured in hours.
You wake up in another region.

title: Platform sellers
text: The train stops for twenty minutes and local people line the platform with pies, smoked fish, potatoes and berries.

choices.then: The potatoes are hot and the pie is better than any restaurant. You return just in time.
The smell reaches you anyway.

title: The neighbour on the lower berth
text: An elderly man on the lower berth starts a conversation with the sentence "And where are you going, young person?"

choices.then: Three hours and one boiled egg later, he has told you about his life and given you advice you will think about for years.
He starts the same conversation with the person opposite.

title: Another time zone
text: The tickets and the station clocks use Moscow time, but outside the window it is clearly night. The Trans-Siberian line, about nine thousand three hundred kilometres from Moscow to Vladivostok, crosses many time zones.

choices.t: Learn the rules from the timetable
choices.then: It takes a while, but you finally work out when you will really arrive.
Your body protests but the day goes on.

title: Left on the platform
text: At a long stop you wander to look at the station and the train begins to move. Your phone and wallet are on the train.

choices.t: Run and jump onto the last carriage
choices.then: The attendant opens the door with a face that says everything. You catch your breath for an hour.
He calls ahead and the next train takes you to the next stop, where your things wait. It costs a day.

title: Night in the carriage
text: It is 3 a.m. The carriage is quiet except for the wheels, a distant snore and the light of a lamp on the table.

choices.t: Stand by the window for an hour
choices.then: Dark forest, then a town with a few yellow lights. The world is big.
The wheels sing a lullaby.

title: Arrival
text: The train slows down. The attendant opens the doors and the first breath of a new city smells of coal, rain and something sweet.

choices.t: Step out and take a deep breath
choices.then: A trip of days ends in a minute. Your legs remember the ground.
Efficient, but you missed the moment.

title: Enrolling in the first grade
text: Your child turns six and a half this year. In 2026 the applications for the nearest school opened on 1 April and for children of its catchment area they close on 30 June; the child must be at least 6 years 6 months and not older than 8 on 1 September.

choices.t: Apply online at the start of April
choices.then: A few clicks, a date and a confirmation. The school is a ten-minute walk away.
You get a place, but the school you wanted fills up.

title: The first of September
text: The "Day of Knowledge": children in white shirts, huge bouquets, a ceremony in the school yard and a first-grader carried on the shoulders of an older boy with a bell.

choices.then: You cry a little and pretend it was the wind. The bell rings and your child is a schoolchild.
A small proud shape in the crowd.

title: The parents' chat
text: You are added to the class parents' chat. By evening there are 143 messages about a lost glove, a collection for a teacher's gift and the correct way to write a date.

choices.then: You become the unofficial organiser of the class tea party.
Peace. You will find out about the gift on the last day.

title: Homework at ten at night
text: Your child has a problem about a train and a pool. Neither of you can remember how to solve it.

choices.then: It takes an hour and a notebook of crossed-out lines. The answer is correct and you are both proud.
She solves it in two minutes and gives a short lecture about ways of thinking.

title: The parents' meeting
text: The teacher calls a meeting. The agenda: behaviour, repairs of the classroom and "voluntary" contributions. Thirty parents sit on small chairs.

choices.then: The meeting lasts two hours. You make friends with another parent over a shared sigh.
The teacher replies with a thumbs-up and a list of tasks.

title: The school clothes
text: The school asks for a uniform or at least "business style": dark trousers or a skirt, a white shirt, indoor shoes. Children grow out of everything by January.

choices.then: Neat, but it is soon too small.

choices.t: Buy second-hand from the class chat
choices.then: A parent hands over a bag with a smile. Not new but perfectly fine.

title: The last bell
text: The "last bell" rings at the end of May and the school year ends with a festive assembly, songs and a speech from the head teacher.

choices.then: A ribbon, a ringing bell, a speech. Summer begins.
They return with photos and a long story.

title: The kindergarten queue
text: You need a place in the kindergarten. The queue is online, and the system tells you your number in a long list, which does not move.

choices.t: Visit the department and ask in person
choices.then: A kind employee finds a way to offer a different kindergarten across the park.

choices.t: Wait and ask a grandmother to help
choices.then: The grandmother takes over with pleasure. Everyone is tired, everyone is happy.

title: The child has a temperature
text: In the morning your child has a fever and a cough. The school says to keep the child at home and bring a note from the doctor.

choices.t: Stay home and call the clinic
choices.then: You read stories under a blanket, make tea with lemon and book an appointment. The child recovers in a few days.

choices.t: Ask a grandmother to come over
choices.then: She arrives with soup in a jar and a firm opinion about medicine.

title: Which number?
text: A neighbour asks whether she should call 112, 101, 102 or 103 when someone falls ill. You realise you are not sure either.

choices.t: Learn the numbers: 112 for everything, 103 for an ambulance
choices.then: The single number 112 works free from any phone and the operator passes the call on. The separate numbers 101, 102, 103 and 104 are also free from a mobile.

choices.t: Say "just google it when it happens"
choices.then: In an emergency, nobody wants to search. You make a note to learn them.

title: Calling with little Russian
text: Your neighbour has collapsed and the line to 112 is answered by a calm voice speaking quickly. Your Russian is limited.

choices.t: Say the address and one word: "ambulance"
choices.then: The operator repeats the address, asks one more question and sends help. Simple words are enough.

choices.t: Hang up and look for a translator app
choices.then: Precious minutes pass before you call again.

title: The smell of smoke on the stairs
text: In the evening you smell smoke in the stairwell. A neighbour shouts "Fire!" from two floors below.

choices.t: Leave by the stairs, call 101 or 112, and knock on doors as you go
choices.then: Everyone is out in the yard in five minutes. The fire crew arrives soon; a pan on a stove, quickly dealt with.

choices.t: Take the lift to the ground floor
choices.then: The lift stops between floors. Waiting is the longest wait of your life; the crew gets you out.

title: A smell of gas
text: In a flat with a gas stove you smell gas. A light switch is within your reach.

choices.t: Open the windows, avoid switches and flames, and call 104 from outside
choices.then: The gas service finds a worn connection and fixes it. The dispatcher thanks you for waiting outside.

choices.t: Switch on the light to look for the source
choices.then: Nothing happens, this time. The dispatcher scolds you on the phone.

title: Someone collapses
text: A man in the metro sits down heavily and does not answer when you ask if he is all right.

choices.t: Check that he is breathing, shout for help and call 103
choices.then: People gather. Someone brings water, a doctor passenger takes over and the ambulance arrives.
Everybody assumes the same for a minute. You then call yourself.

title: A slip on the ice
text: In January you slip on a hidden patch of ice and your wrist hurts badly.

choices.t: Go to the emergency room and get it checked
choices.then: An X-ray shows a small fracture. A plaster, a prescription and three weeks of careful life.

choices.t: Wrap it up and carry on
choices.then: It hurts for a month. A doctor later says you were fortunate.

title: At the pharmacy counter
text: You have a heavy cold. The pharmacist offers a long list of medicines, some of which look very similar.

choices.t: Ask her what is necessary and what is just expensive
choices.then: She picks two simple things and tells you to drink warm liquids. The bill is small.
A bag of boxes and a lighter wallet; the cold goes away on the usual schedule.

title: The lights go out
text: On a winter evening the whole street goes dark. The phone has 20 per cent battery.

choices.t: Check the building chat and call the electricity service
choices.then: Power is back in two hours; a neighbour shares candles and a thermos of tea.

choices.t: Sit in the dark and wait
choices.then: It works eventually. You regret not having a torch.

title: The loyalty card
text: At the till the cashier asks, in one breath: "Do you have the card? The app? A bag? Do you want to collect points?"

choices.t: Install the shop's app and take the card
choices.then: A discount on the first basket and a stream of notifications. You use it in the end.
The cashier smiles and moves on. You pay full price and escape.

title: The yellow sticker
text: In the evening, a shop worker puts yellow discount stickers on bread, milk and ready meals that will expire tomorrow. A small group of regulars is already waiting.

choices.t: Join the regulars and grab a loaf and a pie
choices.then: Half-price dinner, and a wink from the lady next to you.

choices.t: Pay full price for fresh bread
choices.then: It tastes the same and costs twice as much.

title: The self-checkout
text: A self-checkout machine announces "Unexpected item in the bagging area" for the third time. A queue forms behind you.

choices.then: She arrives with a card and a sigh. In two seconds it works.
Slower and calmer. The cashier says "you wouldn't believe how many people do that".

title: Bargaining at the market
text: At a covered market a seller of honey asks for 900 for a jar. People around you taste, nod, and bargain gently.

choices.then: You get a jar and a spoonful of something else for free, at a little less than the first price.
The seller is pleased. You feel the story was not so friendly after all.

title: Weigh it yourself
text: In the vegetable section of the supermarket you must weigh tomatoes at a scale and print a label before you go to the till.

choices.t: Learn the scale and print the label
choices.then: Number, tomatoes, label. You come out with a perfect bag and a small win.
She sends you back; the queue sighs.

title: The jacket does not fit
text: A week ago you bought a jacket that turns out to be one size too small. You still have the tag and the receipt. In general, a non-food item of proper quality may be exchanged within 14 days, not counting the day of purchase, if it has not been used.

choices.t: Go back with the receipt and the tag
choices.then: The clerk checks the label and finds a bigger size. A polite exchange.

choices.t: Keep it and hope to lose weight
choices.then: The jacket waits in the cupboard.

title: Underwear and the list of non-returnable items
text: You bought something in a pharmacy and a pair of socks, and change your mind. The clerk points to the sign: certain categories, such as medicines, personal hygiene items and underwear, are not exchangeable.

choices.t: Read the sign and learn the rule
choices.then: You keep the items and make a note: try things on in the shop next time.
She stays calm and friendly; the list is on the wall.

title: The receipt
text: At the end of a small purchase the cashier tucks the receipt into your bag without a word. A friend says: "Always keep it. And scan the QR code if it needs to be checked."

choices.then: A year later a warranty claim goes smoothly because you found the receipt.
Clean pockets and a lesson learned later.

title: Bring your own bag
text: The cashier asks if you need a bag. At home there are already thirty of them under the sink.

choices.then: The shopping fits. A small win and a small reputation as an eco person.
It is cheap and it ends up under the sink.

title: Paying by QR code
text: At a small market stall there is no card reader, only a printed QR code stuck to the counter. The seller says "by phone, please".

choices.t: Scan and pay with your banking app
choices.then: A second later the seller's phone says "payment received". Easy and cash-free.
You find one at the other end of the street and pay in cash.

title: A marketplace sale
text: An app shows a banner: "Sale! Up to 70 per cent off". Your basket already has a kettle, a lamp and a pair of boots you did not know you needed.

choices.then: It arrives in three days, works and costs less than in the shop.
The boots do not fit, the lamp is the wrong colour and you spend a weekend returning things.

title: The pickup point
text: Your order is ready at a pickup point in a basement beside the pharmacy. The assistant asks for the code from the app and brings out four bags.

choices.t: Open the bag and check it at the counter
choices.then: Everything is as ordered. The assistant nods approvingly: "That is the right way."
At home you discover that the lid is missing. You will need the app after all.

title: Trying on at the pickup point
text: You ordered two sizes of the same jacket. The pickup point has a curtain in the corner and a queue behind you.

choices.t: Try both quickly and keep one
choices.then: The right size fits like a glove. The other goes back in the bag.

choices.t: Take both home and decide later
choices.then: You return one next week and get your money back after a few days.

title: Returning an item
text: A pair of headphones stopped working after a week. The app has a button "Return" and a form with five reasons.

choices.t: Fill in the form with a photo of the fault
choices.then: A courier takes it, and a few days later the money returns to your card.
They sit in the drawer and judge you.

title: A slip from the post
text: A paper notice in the mailbox says a parcel is waiting at the post office. The slip is hand-written and the post office is across the district.

choices.t: Go with a passport and wait in the queue
choices.then: The queue is long but the parcel is waiting. The clerk checks the passport three times and hands it over with a smile.
The parcel is returned to the sender on the last day. You wonder who sent it.

title: The courier is calling
text: The courier calls and says in one breath: "I am at your entrance, the code is not working, which floor is it?"

choices.then: Two minutes, a smile and a signature. The courier thanks you for not making him climb.

choices.t: Talk him through the entrance code
choices.then: Eventually he finds the right button and reaches the fifth floor.

title: A message about a parcel you did not order
text: An SMS says your parcel is held at customs and asks you to pay a small fee through a link.

choices.t: Delete it and check the real order list in the app
choices.then: There is nothing in the app. You block the number and feel a little clever.

choices.t: Click the link just to see
choices.then: The page looks suspicious and you close it at once. A good moment to remember the scam rules.

title: A gift from afar
text: A relative from your home town has sent a parcel by post: jars, dried herbs, a woollen scarf and a letter. The box has travelled a week.

choices.t: Open it slowly and call to say thank you
choices.then: The scarf is itchy and perfect. The call lasts an hour.

choices.t: Open it and send a message
choices.then: A quick "thank you" and a photo. It is received with a heart.

title: The barber
text: A small barbershop at the corner has a cat on the windowsill and a sign "Walk-ins welcome". The barber asks: "As usual?" although you have never been here.

choices.then: You leave with a decent haircut and a warm feeling of being a regular.
He studies it for a long time and says it will be "close". It is.

title: The shoe repair stall
text: The sole of your boot has come away. At a stall in the underpass a man in an apron looks at it for two seconds. "Fifteen minutes."

choices.then: He glues, presses and polishes. The boots are better than new and you hear a story about the 1990s.
Expensive, but that is that.

title: Duplicating a key
text: You have lost your spare key and the landlord says "make a copy". There is a key-cutting booth next to the metro, with a machine that screams.

choices.then: A shower of metal sparks and two shiny keys in two minutes.
You lose it within a week.

title: The tailor's studio
text: Your only decent jacket is a size too big. A tailor in a basement studio pins it, tuts, and pins again.

choices.then: A week later it fits like it was made for you.
The sleeves cover your hands. People say it is "oversize style".

title: The dry cleaner
text: A friend's wine has met your coat. The dry cleaner looks at the stain, at you, and says: "It will come out. Probably."

choices.then: The coat is clean and smells faintly of citrus. A good decision.
The stain fades but the colour does too.

title: The phone-screen kiosk
text: You dropped your phone and the screen is a spider's web. A kiosk in the mall offers "repair while you wait, one year warranty".

choices.then: Forty minutes later the phone is almost like new and the warranty paper is in your pocket.
You cut your thumb twice and your phone looks like a map.

title: The laundromat
text: The washing machine at home has broken. A self-service laundromat opens at the end of the street, and a woman at the next machine offers you detergent.

choices.then: Two hours, tea from a vending machine and a long conversation about the price of everything.

choices.t: Wash in the bath by hand
choices.then: Your arms ache and your jeans are cleaner than they have been in months.

title: The copy shop
text: An office asks for a "notarised-looking" copy of your documents. At a copy shop the girl behind the counter says: "Black and white or colour? How many sets? Do you need them stapled?"

choices.then: Nine pages, a stapler and a polite thank you. The office does not ask for another set.
The office asks for two more copies. You return.

title: You do not have a business yet
text: You daydream about a stand of your own. Starting one takes money, a tax registration and nerves. Use 💻 Online services → "Register a business" to open the registration form.

choices.then: You open a notebook and start listing costs.

title: A health & safety inspection
text: Two inspectors in grey jackets walk in: "Documents, sanitary book, receipts."

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: The supplier raises prices
text: Your main supplier sends a message: "Prices go up 15% from Monday."

choices.t: Negotiate and switch part of the order
choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: A bad review goes viral
text: A customer posts: "Never again!" with a blurry photo. Fifty people share it.

choices.t: Reply politely and offer to fix the problem
choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: You need help: hire someone?
text: Orders are piling up. A friend recommends a worker looking for a job.

choices.t: Hire him with a proper contract
choices.then: You no longer run a business.

choices.t: Hire him informally, cash in hand
choices.then: You no longer run a business.

title: You cannot hire as self-employed
text: A customer offers to send his nephew to help you. As self-employed you may not employ staff.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: Your equipment breaks
text: The oven (or the printer, or the soldering iron) dies with a puff of smoke.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: A rush of customers
text: A local festival brings crowds to your door.

choices.t: Work flat out for two days
choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: A competitor opens next door
text: A bigger brand opens across the street with banners and discounts.

choices.t: Compete on service and loyalty cards
choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: Tax reminder
text: A push notification: "Your tax payment is ready. Pay by the 28th." Receipts, apps and a deadline.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: A suspicious bulk order
text: A "customer from abroad" wants a large order and asks you to pay "a transfer fee" first.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: A local journalist visits
text: A reporter from the district paper is writing about small businesses.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: Expand the business?
text: A bigger place opens up on the same street. Double the space, double the rent.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: Close the business?
text: Weeks of thin profits make you doubt. A buyer offers a fair price.

choices.then: You no longer run a business.
You no longer run a business.

title: Checking a worker's papers
text: A new worker hands you a passport and a patent. They look in order, but the date has passed.

choices.t: Check the patent dates and ask for a valid one
choices.then: You no longer run a business.

choices.t: Ignore it, you need the hands
choices.then: You no longer run a business.

title: Timur moves in
text: A new roommate arrives with a duffel bag, a rice cooker and a big smile. "I am Timur. I work nights. I promise I am quiet."

choices.then: Plov from his rice cooker, tea from yours. By midnight you are friends.
Rules on a sheet of paper: dishes, quiet hours, guests. He signs with a flourish.

title: Late-night calls to his mother
text: Every night at 2 a.m. Timur whispers into his phone. You hear a mother's voice, tinny and warm, asking if he has eaten.

choices.t: Offer him the kitchen so he can talk freely
choices.then: He is moved. The next day there is a pot of lagman waiting for you.
He nods and speaks in whispers. Awkward but fine.

title: Timur loses his night job
text: Timur sits on his bunk, staring at his phone. "They let me go. I do not know how I will pay my share this week."
